motivation: To develop quantum error-correcting codes that require fewer resources for fault-tolerant quantum computation, specifically codes that can correct errors in a single round of syndrome extraction.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot error correction properties.
result: The proposed codes achieve single-shot fault tolerance with significantly shorter block lengths compared to previous codes, and have a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1%.
conclusion: These codes offer a promising avenue for reducing overhead in fault-tolerant quantum computing, though further work is needed to assess practical implementation and performance under realistic noise models.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and realistic experimental tools.
motivation: To develop a general and efficient protocol for preparing multimode multi-photon quantum states, which is a key resource for quantum information processing.
method: The authors use symmetric tensor decomposition to decompose any photonic state into a sequence of operations that can be implemented with current experimental platforms.
result: They show that every photonic state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps using realistic tools.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic approach to photonic state preparation, potentially advancing quantum computing and communication experiments.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant quantum computation of molecular energies using error-corrected logical qubits on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated into practical quantum chemistry simulations, improving accuracy despite hardware noise.
method: Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets were employed on a trapped-ion quantum processor to compute molecular energies.
result: The computation achieved improved accuracy compared to non-error-corrected approaches, demonstrating the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum chemistry.
conclusion: The work paves the way for larger-scale error-corrected quantum simulations, though further improvements in logical gate fidelities are needed.

title: Quantum Filtering And Analysis Of Multiplicities In Eigenvalue Spectra
authors: Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, And Ruizhe Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, and Ruizhe Zhang

A quantum filtering algorithm identifies clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020318] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: A quantum filtering algorithm for identifying eigenvalue clusters and multiplicities in spectral analysis.
motivation: To overcome worst-case complexity barriers in classical spectral analysis by leveraging quantum algorithms.
method: Quantum filtering techniques that estimate eigenvalue multiplicities and cluster locations.
result: The algorithm efficiently identifies clusters and multiplicities, offering advantages over classical methods.
conclusion: Provides a new quantum tool for spectral analysis with potential applications in quantum computing and numerical linear algebra.

title: Fault-Tolerant Operations In Majorana-Based Quantum Codes: Gates, Measurements, And High-Rate Constructions
authors: Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, and Daniel Gottesman

By generalizing from qubit error correction, fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic processes are created, which enable gates, measurements, and codes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020315] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops fault-tolerant protocols for Majorana-based quantum codes, focusing on gates, measurements, and high-rate code constructions.
motivation: To extend fault-tolerant quantum error correction techniques from qubit systems to fermionic systems, specifically Majorana-based codes, which are promising for topological quantum computing.
method: Generalization of qubit fault-tolerant protocols to fermionic processes, including design of transversal gates, error correction procedures, and high-rate code constructions.
result: Creation of fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic systems, enabling gates and measurements in Majorana-based codes with improved rates.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for fault-tolerant quantum computing with Majorana fermions, with implications for topological quantum computation and error correction.

title: Simulating Quantum Circuits With Arbitrary Local Noise Using Pauli Propagation
authors: Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, and Zoë Holmes

Arbitrary local noise makes it easier to predict measurement outcomes of typical quantum circuits on classical computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020313] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that arbitrary local noise makes quantum circuits easier to simulate classically via Pauli propagation.
motivation: To understand the impact of noise on classical simulability of quantum circuits, which is important for benchmarking and error mitigation.
method: The authors develop a Pauli propagation method to simulate quantum circuits under arbitrary local noise, analyzing the computational cost.
result: Arbitrary local noise reduces the effective circuit depth, enabling efficient classical simulation of typical circuits.
conclusion: Noisy quantum circuits may lose quantum advantage; the method provides a tool for assessing classical simulability.

title: High-Threshold, Low-Overhead And Single-Shot Decodable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Memory
authors: Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, And Joschka Roffe
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, and Joschka Roffe

Radial codes, a new class of low-density parity-check codes with strong error correction capabilities, tunable parameters, and small size, are shown to be a promising candidate for near-term quantum devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020310] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Radial codes are introduced as a new class of low-density parity-check codes offering high threshold, low overhead, and single-shot decodable fault-tolerant quantum memory.
motivation: To develop quantum error-correcting codes that are practical for near-term devices, balancing strong error correction with small size and tunable parameters.
method: The authors propose radial codes, a family of LDPC codes, and analyze their performance in terms of threshold, overhead, and single-shot decoding capability.
result: Radial codes achieve high error thresholds, low qubit overhead, and can be decoded in a single shot, making them promising for fault-tolerant quantum memory.
conclusion: Radial codes are a strong candidate for near-term quantum devices, but further work is needed to assess their compatibility with specific hardware and to develop efficient decoders.

title: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks Are Effectively Classically Simulable
authors: Pablo Bermejo, Paolo Braccia, Manuel S. Rudolph, Zoë Holmes, Lukasz Cincio, And M. Cerezo
abstract:
Author(s): Pablo Bermejo, Paolo Braccia, Manuel S. Rudolph, Zoë Holmes, Lukasz Cincio, and M. Cerezo

The action of a quantum convolutional neural network, which is a promising architecture for quantum machine learning, can be efficiently simulated by a classical computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020304] Published Mon Apr 06, 2026.
tldr: Quantum convolutional neural networks can be efficiently simulated classically, challenging their quantum advantage.
motivation: To determine whether quantum convolutional neural networks offer a computational advantage over classical methods.
method: The authors likely analyze the structure of QCNNs and prove that their action can be simulated efficiently on a classical computer, possibly using tensor network or other classical simulation techniques.
result: QCNNs are effectively classically simulable, meaning they do not provide a quantum advantage for the tasks considered.
conclusion: The findings suggest that QCNNs may not be a viable candidate for near-term quantum advantage, and alternative quantum machine learning architectures should be explored.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism since its experimental realization in 2016.
method: Review article summarizing experimental and theoretical progress in 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and multiferroics.
conclusion: The field is rapidly evolving, expanding theoretical understanding and opening new application directions.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This review unifies the description of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics, focusing on local energy, momentum, and spin densities.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of how wave fields exert forces and torques on particles, a topic with applications in trapping, manipulation, and sorting.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes theoretical frameworks and experimental results from optics and acoustics, emphasizing a unified perspective based on local densities.
result: It covers applications such as optical trapping, acoustic sorting, and pulling forces, and highlights the role of spin and momentum densities.
conclusion: The review offers a unified understanding of radiation forces and torques, with implications for particle manipulation and future studies in wave-matter interactions.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics using brickwork quantum circuits, focusing on exactly solvable models.
motivation: To provide a pedagogical overview of how space-time duality and quantum circuit analogies can simplify the computation of quantum many-body dynamics.
method: Review of theoretical framework based on space-time duality in discrete lattice systems, with emphasis on brickwork quantum circuits.
result: Unified view of dynamical evolution in many-body systems via space-time duality, linking to quantum computation.
conclusion: The approach offers a powerful tool for studying quantum dynamics, but the paper is a review and does not present new results directly applicable to the user's specific interests.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: This review covers exotic electronic states in kagome metals, focusing on topological flat bands, Dirac fermions, and unconventional superconductivity.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena observed in kagome metals, driven by frustrated geometry and strong correlations.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic states including unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism, and electronic nematicity.
conclusion: The review elucidates key mechanisms and suggests future directions for exploring correlated and topological physics in these materials.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: This pedagogical review applies field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying diverse approaches for modeling complex systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems using field-theoretic methods, which are powerful but often scattered across different disciplines.
method: The authors review and apply field-theoretic methods, including path integrals and Doi-Peliti formalism, to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how field theories can unify various approaches to reaction-diffusion systems, offering a systematic way to handle fluctuations and correlations.
conclusion: The methods have broad applicability beyond chemistry, such as in ecology and epidemiology, and provide a foundation for further theoretical developments.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: This review updates the field of spin glasses, covering experiment, theory, and simulations, with emphasis on their synergy.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass dynamics and highlight the interplay between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: Review of existing literature and synthesis of experimental, theoretical, and large-scale simulation results.
result: The paper tracks progress in spin-glass research and identifies future opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation is essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: This review covers theoretical and experimental progress on Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of Kitaev spin liquids, which are a paradigmatic example of quantum spin liquids with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials like α-RuCl3, discussing techniques such as neutron scattering and thermal transport.
result: Key findings include the identification of candidate materials, observation of fractionalized excitations, and chiral edge modes, confirming predictions of the Kitaev model.
conclusion: The review highlights open questions and future directions, such as realizing a true quantum spin liquid ground state and exploring device applications.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze large-scale neural recordings, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how coordinated neural activity in the brain can be described using principles from statistical physics.
method: Review of recent experiments recording electrical activity from thousands of neurons, analyzed with maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques.
result: Statistical physics models can quantitatively reproduce neural activity patterns and reveal reproducible behaviors.
conclusion: Abstract theoretical principles from physics can achieve predictive power in neuroscience, similar to other areas of physics.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: This review covers theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions relevant to photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of theoretical approaches describing internal conversion, a key photophysical process, and to guide applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper is a review that surveys various theoretical models for internal conversion, including quantum dynamics and rate theories.
result: The review summarizes the state of the art in modeling internal conversion and discusses how these models can be integrated into applied research.
conclusion: The authors suggest that improved theoretical methods can enhance the design of materials for photonics and energy harvesting, but the paper does not present new results.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of nonequilibrium dynamics in photoexcited Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and photoinduced phase transitions.
motivation: To understand and control material properties using light in strongly correlated systems, exploring novel optical responses and metastable phases.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing nonlinear and nonperturbative driving pathways.
result: Key mechanisms for photodoped carrier evolution and emergence of metastable orders (superconducting, magnetic, orbital, excitonic) are highlighted.
conclusion: Provides a framework for future research in nonequilibrium strongly correlated systems, with potential for material control and quantum metastable phases.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum-mechanical aspects of magnetic skyrmions, including their formation interactions and quantum features.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of quantum properties of magnetic skyrmions, which have been studied mainly classically, and to highlight their potential for quantum technologies.
method: Review article summarizing theoretical and experimental progress on quantum skyrmions, covering topological aspects, quantum dynamics, and interactions.
result: Discusses quantum tunneling, superposition, and entanglement of skyrmions, as well as quantum effects in skyrmion formation.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmions may enable new quantum technologies, but many open questions remain regarding their observation and control.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their potential connection to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To systematically survey the landscape of spin-dependent forces mediated by exotic bosons, which could reveal new physics beyond the Standard Model and shed light on dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper is a review that summarizes theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent interactions (e.g., from axions, Z' bosons) and surveys experimental techniques such as atomic magnetometry, torsion balances, and spin-precession experiments.
result: The review catalogs numerous experimental constraints on spin-dependent couplings and discusses the implications for discrete symmetry violations and dark matter candidates.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, with many experimental bounds improving but no definitive detection yet; future experiments with increased sensitivity are needed.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to simplify multiqubit gate decompositions and realize quantum algorithms, with a focus on experimental implementations.
motivation: To survey the potential advantages of qudits over qubits in quantum computing, particularly for reducing circuit complexity and resource requirements.
method: The paper provides a review of theoretical proposals and experimental demonstrations of qudit-based quantum computing, including qudit-qubit embeddings and gate decompositions.
result: Qudits can simplify certain multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli gate) and reduce the number of operations, but practical challenges remain in qudit control and coherence.
conclusion: Qudits offer a promising alternative for quantum computing, but further experimental progress is needed to realize their full potential.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on physical properties due to violations of underlying assumptions in measurement contexts.
motivation: To clarify why some measurements exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and to explore how materials can be designed to violate these assumptions for enhanced properties.
method: A review of various experimental and theoretical cases where measured properties exceed classical bounds, analyzing which assumptions are violated.
result: Many apparent violations arise from non-equilibrium conditions, inhomogeneities, or other deviations from the assumptions of classical thermodynamics.
conclusion: Understanding these violations can lead to the development of materials with superior properties, but the findings do not challenge fundamental thermodynamics.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data up to the end of 2022.
motivation: To provide an updated, self-consistent set of fundamental constants for use in science and technology, reflecting the latest experimental and theoretical improvements.
method: A least-squares adjustment that combines data from various experiments and theoretical calculations, taking into account correlations and uncertainties.
result: A new set of recommended values for fundamental constants and conversion factors, with improved precision compared to previous adjustments.
conclusion: The updated constants are essential for accurate measurements and theoretical calculations across physics and chemistry, and the methodology continues to evolve with new data.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the current ability to predict spin coherence times using ab initio methods, which is crucial for quantum technologies.
method: Review of cluster expansion techniques and other computational approaches for calculating spin-spin relaxation times, with discussion of higher-order perturbations and surface effects.
result: Cluster expansion methods yield reliable predictions for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for cases involving higher-order perturbations and decoherence from surfaces/interfaces.
conclusion: The field is maturing, with predictive capabilities improving, but further development is needed to handle complex decoherence mechanisms.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental and theoretical progress in realizing quantum many-body systems on fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions using atomic, photonic, and electronic platforms.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries that enable simulation of topological phenomena and gravitational/cosmological models.
method: Review of experimental implementations (cold atoms, photonic lattices, electronic systems) and theoretical frameworks for synthetic quantum matter in fractal, curved, and higher-dimensional geometries.
result: Summarizes key achievements in engineering fractal lattices, synthetic curved spaces, and synthetic dimensions, and discusses emergent phenomena such as topological states and analog gravity.
conclusion: These synthetic platforms open new avenues for studying quantum many-body physics beyond conventional geometries, with implications for condensed matter, quantum simulation, and fundamental physics.

title: Quantum Cellular Automata On Symmetric Subalgebras
authors: Ruochen Ma, Yabo Li, And Meng Cheng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2123 (2026).

We investigate quantum cellular automata (QCA) on one-dimensional spin systems defined over a subalgebra of the full local operator algebra – the symmetric subalgebra under a finite Abelian group symmetry [MATH]. For systems where each site carries a regular representation of [MATH], we establish a complete classification of such subalgebra QCAs based on two topological invariants: (1) a surjective homomorphism from the group of subalgebra QCAs to the group of anyon permutation symmetries in a [MATH] [MATH] gauge theory; and (2) a generalization of the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index that characterizes the flow of the symmetric subalgebra. Specifically, two subalgebra QCAs correspond to the same anyon permutation and share the same index if and only if they differ by a finite-depth unitary circuit composed of [MATH]-symmetric local gates. We also identify a set of operations that generate all subalgebra QCAs through finite compositions. As an example, we examine the Kramers-Wannier duality on a [MATH] symmetric subalgebra, demonstrating that it maps to the [MATH]-[MATH] permutation in the two-dimensional toric code and has an irrational index of [MATH]. Therefore, it cannot be extended to a QCA over the full local operator algebra and mixes nontrivially with lattice translations.

.
tldr: This paper classifies quantum cellular automata on symmetric subalgebras of one-dimensional spin systems with finite Abelian group symmetry, using topological invariants and a generalized index.
motivation: To understand the structure and classification of quantum cellular automata that respect a given symmetry, which is important for understanding topological phases and dualities.
method: The authors define subalgebra QCAs on the symmetric subalgebra of a finite Abelian group symmetry, and classify them using a homomorphism to anyon permutations in the corresponding gauge theory and a generalization of the GNVW index.
result: They establish a complete classification: two subalgebra QCAs are equivalent up to finite-depth symmetric circuits iff they have the same anyon permutation and index. They also show the Kramers-Wannier duality corresponds to a nontrivial anyon permutation and has an irrational index.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous classification of symmetric QCAs, revealing that some dualities (like Kramers-Wannier) cannot be extended to full algebra QCAs and mix nontrivially with translations.

title: Squeezing Enhancement In Lossy Multi-Path Atom Interferometers
authors: Julian Günther, Jan-Niclas Kirsten-Siemß, Naceur Gaaloul, And Klemens Hammerer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2122 (2026).

This paper explores the sensitivity gains afforded by spin-squeezed states in atom interferometry, in particular using Bragg diffraction. We introduce a generalised input-output formalism that accurately describes realistic, non-unitary interferometers, including losses due to velocity selectivity and scattering into undesired momentum states. This formalism is applied to evaluate the performance of one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states in improving phase sensitivity. Our results show that by carefully optimising the parameters of the Bragg beam splitters and controlling the degree of squeezing, it is possible to improve the sensitivity of the interferometer by several dB with respect to the standard quantum limit despite realistic levels of losses in light pulse operations. However, the analysis also highlights the challenges associated with achieving these improvements in practice, most notably the impact of finite temperature on the benefits of entanglement. The results suggest ways of optimising interferometric setups to exploit quantum entanglement under realistic conditions, thereby contributing to advances in precision metrology with atom interferometers.

.
tldr: This paper studies spin-squeezed states in lossy atom interferometers to enhance phase sensitivity, but does not directly address the user's research interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, quantum communication, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To improve sensitivity in atom interferometry beyond the standard quantum limit using quantum entanglement, despite realistic losses.
method: Generalized input-output formalism for non-unitary interferometers, applied to one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states with Bragg diffraction.
result: Optimized squeezing and beam splitter parameters can yield several dB improvement over the standard quantum limit, but finite temperature reduces benefits.
conclusion: Provides guidelines for exploiting entanglement in practical atom interferometers, advancing precision metrology.

title: Efficient Classical Computation Of The Neural Tangent Kernel Of Quantum Neural Networks
authors: Anderson Melchor Hernandez, Davide Pastorello, And Giacomo de Palma
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2118 (2026).

We propose an efficient classical algorithm to estimate the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) associated with a broad class of quantum neural networks. These networks consist of arbitrary unitary operators belonging to the Clifford group interleaved with parametric gates given by the time evolution generated by an arbitrary Hamiltonian belonging to the Pauli group. The proposed algorithm leverages a key insight: the average over the distribution of initialization parameters in the NTK definition can be exactly replaced by an average over just four discrete values, chosen such that the corresponding parametric gates are Clifford operations. This reduction enables an efficient classical simulation of the circuit. Combined with recent results establishing the equivalence between wide quantum neural networks and Gaussian processes [Girardi et al., Comm. Math. Phys. 406, 92 (2025); Melchor Hernandez et al., Ann. Henri Poincaré (2025)], our method enables efficient computation of the expected output of wide, trained quantum neural networks, and therefore shows that such networks cannot achieve quantum advantage.

.
tldr: This paper shows that the neural tangent kernel of certain quantum neural networks can be computed classically, implying no quantum advantage for wide, trained QNNs.
motivation: To determine whether quantum neural networks can offer a computational advantage over classical methods, specifically by analyzing their training dynamics via the neural tangent kernel.
method: The authors replace the average over initialization parameters in the NTK with an average over four discrete Clifford operations, enabling efficient classical simulation of the circuit.
result: The NTK for a broad class of QNNs (Clifford + Pauli-generated gates) can be computed classically in polynomial time, and combined with Gaussian process equivalence, the expected output of wide trained QNNs is classically tractable.
conclusion: Such quantum neural networks cannot achieve quantum advantage, and the work provides a classical algorithm to simulate them efficiently.

title: Hidden Time-nonlocal Floquet Symmetries
authors: Sigmund Kohler And Jesús Casado-Pascual
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2112 (2026).

We investigate the Floquet spectrum of a detuned, driven two-level system and show that it exhibits exact quasienergy crossings when the detuning is an integer multiple of the energy quantum of the driving field. This behavior can be explained by a hidden time-nonlocal parity, which allows the Floquet modes to be classified as even or odd. Then a generic feature is the emergence of exact crossings between quasienergies of different parity. A constructive proof of the existence of the symmetry is based on a scalar recurrence relation. Moreover, we present a general scheme for its numerical computation, which can be applied to models beyond the two-level system. Analytical results are illustrated with numerical data.

.
tldr: The paper discovers hidden time-nonlocal Floquet symmetries in driven two-level systems that explain exact quasienergy crossings.
motivation: To understand the origin of exact quasienergy crossings in periodically driven quantum systems, which are not explained by standard symmetries.
method: Analytical derivation using a scalar recurrence relation and numerical computation of the hidden symmetry.
result: Exact quasienergy crossings occur when detuning is an integer multiple of the driving frequency, classified by a hidden time-nonlocal parity.
conclusion: The hidden symmetry is generic and can be extended to other Floquet systems, offering a new tool for analyzing driven quantum systems.

title: Operator Space Fragmentation In Perturbed Floquet-Clifford Circuits
authors: Marcell D. Kovács, Christopher J. Turner, Lluis Masanes, And Arijeet Pal
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2107 (2026).

Floquet quantum circuits are able to realise a wide range of non-equilibrium quantum states, exhibiting quantum chaos, topological order and localisation. In this work, we investigate the stability of operator localisation and emergence of chaos in random Floquet-Clifford circuits subjected to unitary perturbations which drive them away from the Clifford limit. We construct a nearest-neighbour Clifford circuit with a brickwork pattern and study the effect of including disordered non-Clifford gates. The perturbations are uniformly sampled from single-qubit unitaries with probability [MATH] on each qubit. We show that the interacting model exhibits strong localisation of operators for [MATH] that is characterised by the fragmentation of operator space into disjoint sectors due to the appearance of wall configurations. Such walls give rise to emergent local integrals of motion for the circuit that we construct exactly. We analytically establish the stability of localisation against generic perturbations and calculate the average length of operator spreading tunable by [MATH]. Although our circuit is not separable across any bi-partition, we further show that the operator localisation leads to an entanglement bottleneck, where initially unentangled states remain weakly entangled across typical fragment boundaries. Finally, we study the spectral form factor (SFF) to characterise the chaotic properties of the operator fragments and spectral fluctuations as a probe of non-ergodicity. In the [MATH] model, the emergence of a fragmentation time scale is found before random matrix theory sets in after which the SFF can be approximated by that of the circular unitary ensemble. Our work provides an explicit description of quantum phases in operator dynamics and circuit ergodicity which can be realised on current NISQ devices.

.
tldr: This paper studies operator space fragmentation and localization in perturbed Floquet-Clifford circuits, revealing emergent integrals of motion and entanglement bottlenecks.
motivation: To understand the stability of operator localization and the emergence of chaos in quantum circuits when perturbed away from the Clifford limit.
method: The authors construct a nearest-neighbour Clifford circuit with a brickwork pattern and add disordered non-Clifford gates uniformly sampled from single-qubit unitaries. They analyze operator spreading, fragmentation, and spectral form factor analytically and numerically.
result: They find strong operator localization for small perturbation probability, characterized by fragmentation into disjoint sectors due to wall configurations, and show that this leads to an entanglement bottleneck. The spectral form factor exhibits a fragmentation time scale before random matrix theory behavior sets in.
conclusion: The work provides an explicit description of quantum phases in operator dynamics and circuit ergodicity, with potential realization on NISQ devices, but does not directly address the user's specific research interests.

title: Polynomial Time Constructive Decision Algorithm For Multivariable Quantum Signal Processing
authors: Yuki Ito, Hitomi Mori, Kazuki Sakamoto, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2102 (2026).

Quantum signal processing (QSP) and quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) have provided a unified framework for understanding many quantum algorithms, including factorization, matrix inversion, and Hamiltonian simulation. As a multivariable version of QSP, multivariable quantum signal processing (M-QSP) is proposed. M-QSP interleaves signal operators corresponding to each variable with signal processing operators, which provides an efficient means to perform multivariable polynomial transformations. However, the necessary and sufficient condition for what types of polynomials can be constructed by M-QSP is unknown. In this paper, we propose a classical algorithm to determine whether a given pair of multivariable Laurent polynomials can be implemented by M-QSP, which returns True or False. As one of the most important properties of this algorithm, its returning True is the necessary and sufficient condition. The proposed classical algorithm runs in polynomial time in the number of variables and signal operators. Our algorithm also provides a constructive method to select the necessary parameters for implementing M-QSP. These findings offer valuable insights for identifying practical applications of M-QSP.

.
tldr: This paper presents a polynomial-time classical algorithm to decide whether a given pair of multivariable Laurent polynomials can be implemented by multivariable quantum signal processing (M-QSP).
motivation: The necessary and sufficient condition for polynomial implementability in M-QSP was unknown, limiting its practical application.
method: The authors propose a classical algorithm that checks the condition and returns True/False, running in polynomial time in the number of variables and signal operators.
result: The algorithm provides a necessary and sufficient condition for M-QSP implementability and also constructs the required parameters.
conclusion: This work enables systematic identification of applications for M-QSP, advancing quantum algorithm design.

title: Construction And Decoding Of Quantum Margulis Codes
authors: Michele Pacenti, Dimitris Chytas, And Bane Vasić
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2101 (2026).

Quantum low-density parity-check codes are a promising approach to fault-tolerant quantum computation, offering potential advantages in rate and decoding efficiency. In this work, we introduce quantum Margulis codes, a new class of QLDPC codes derived from Margulis' classical LDPC construction via the two-block group algebra framework. We show that quantum Margulis codes, unlike bivariate bicycle codes which require ordered statistics decoding for effective error correction, can be efficiently decoded using a standard min-sum decoder with linear complexity, when decoded under the code capacity noise model. This is attributed to their Tanner graph structure, which does not exhibit group symmetry, thereby mitigating the well-known problem of error degeneracy in QLDPC decoding. To further enhance performance, we propose an algorithm for constructing 2BGA codes with controlled girth, ensuring a minimum girth of 6 or 8, and use it to generate several quantum Margulis codes of length 240 and 642. We validate our approach through numerical simulations, demonstrating that quantum Margulis codes behave significantly better than BB codes in the error floor region, under min-sum decoding.

.
tldr: This paper introduces quantum Margulis codes, a new class of QLDPC codes with efficient min-sum decoding, but is not directly related to the user's research interests.
motivation: To construct QLDPC codes that avoid error degeneracy and can be decoded efficiently without ordered statistics decoding.
method: Derived from Margulis' classical LDPC construction via the two-block group algebra framework, with an algorithm to control girth.
result: Quantum Margulis codes achieve better error floor performance than bivariate bicycle codes under min-sum decoding.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical alternative for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but the work is focused on coding theory rather than the user's areas.

title: Learning Symmetry-protected Topological Order From Trapped-ion Experiments
authors: Nicolas Sadoune, Ivan Pogorelov, Claire L. Edmunds, Giuliano Giudici, Giacomo Giudice, Christian D. Marciniak, Martin Ringbauer, Thomas Monz, And Lode Pollet
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2100 (2026).

Classical machine learning has proven remarkably useful in post-processing quantum data, yet typical learning algorithms often require prior training to be effective. In this work, we employ a tensorial kernel support vector machine (TK-SVM) to analyze experimental data produced by trapped-ion quantum computers. This unsupervised method benefits from directly interpretable training parameters, allowing it to identify the non-trivial string-order characterizing symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases. We apply our technique to two examples: a spin-1/2 model and a spin-1 model, featuring the cluster state and the AKLT state as paradigmatic instances of SPT order, respectively. Using matrix product states, we generate a family of quantum circuits that host a trivial phase and an SPT phase, with a sharp phase transition between them. For the spin-1 case, we implement these circuits on two distinct trapped-ion machines based on qubits and qutrits. Our results demonstrate that the TK-SVM method successfully distinguishes the two phases across all noisy experimental datasets, highlighting its robustness and effectiveness in quantum data interpretation.

.
tldr: This paper uses a tensorial kernel support vector machine (TK-SVM) to identify symmetry-protected topological order from trapped-ion quantum computer data.
motivation: To demonstrate that unsupervised machine learning can directly interpret experimental quantum data and identify topological phases without prior training.
method: The authors employ a TK-SVM on data from trapped-ion quantum computers, using matrix product states to generate circuits hosting trivial and SPT phases for spin-1/2 and spin-1 models.
result: The TK-SVM successfully distinguishes trivial and SPT phases across noisy experimental datasets from qubit and qutrit trapped-ion machines.
conclusion: The method is robust and effective for quantum data interpretation, with potential applications in identifying quantum phases from experimental data.

title: Efficient Implementation Of Single Particle Hamiltonians In Exponentially Reduced Qubit Space
authors: Martin Plesch, Martin Friák, And Ijaz Ahamed Mohammad
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2099 (2026).

Current and near-term quantum hardware is constrained by limited qubit counts, circuit depth, and the high cost of repeated measurements. We address these challenges for solid-state Hamiltonians by introducing a logarithmic-qubit encoding that maps a system with [MATH] physical sites onto only [MATH] qubits while maintaining a clear correspondence with the underlying physical model. Within this reduced register, we construct a compatible variational circuit and a Gray-code-inspired measurement strategy whose number of global settings grows only logarithmically with system size. To quantify the overall hardware load, we introduce a volumetric efficiency metric that combines the number of qubits, circuit depth, and the number of measurement settings into a single measure, expressing the overall computation costs. Using this metric, we show that the total space--time sampling volume required in a variational loop can be reduced dramatically from [MATH] to [MATH] for a hardware-efficient ansatz, allowing an exponential reduction in time and size of the quantum hardware. These results demonstrate that large, structured solid-state Hamiltonians can be simulated on substantially smaller quantum registers with controlled sampling overhead and manageable circuit complexity, extending the reach of variational quantum algorithms on near-term devices.

.
tldr: The paper proposes a logarithmic-qubit encoding for simulating single-particle solid-state Hamiltonians on near-term quantum devices, drastically reducing qubit count and measurement settings.
motivation: Current quantum hardware is limited by qubit count, circuit depth, and measurement overhead, hindering simulation of large solid-state systems.
method: A logarithmic encoding maps N physical sites to log N qubits, combined with a variational circuit and Gray-code measurement strategy to reduce measurement settings logarithmically.
result: The total space-time sampling volume is reduced from O(N^2) to O(log^2 N) for a hardware-efficient ansatz, enabling exponential reduction in hardware requirements.
conclusion: The approach extends the reach of variational quantum algorithms for structured Hamiltonians, but is limited to single-particle systems and may not directly apply to many-body or entanglement-related problems.

title: The Complexity Of Local Stoquastic Hamiltonians On 2d Lattices
authors: Gabriel Waite And Michael J. Bremner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2097 (2026).

We show the 2-Local Stoquastic Hamiltonian problem on a 2D square qubit lattice is StoqMA-complete. We achieve this by extending the spatially sparse circuit construction of Oliveira and Terhal, as well as the perturbative gadgets of Bravyi, DiVincenzo, Oliveira, and Terhal. Our main contributions demonstrate StoqMA circuits can be made spatially sparse and that geometrical, stoquastic-preserving, perturbative gadgets can be constructed, without an increase to particle dimension.

.
tldr: This paper proves that the 2-Local Stoquastic Hamiltonian problem on a 2D square lattice is StoqMA-complete, using spatially sparse circuits and perturbative gadgets.
motivation: To understand the computational complexity of stoquastic Hamiltonians, which are relevant to quantum Monte Carlo methods and adiabatic quantum computing.
method: Extends the spatially sparse circuit construction of Oliveira and Terhal and the perturbative gadgets of Bravyi et al., showing StoqMA circuits can be made spatially sparse and that geometrical stoquastic-preserving perturbative gadgets exist without increasing particle dimension.
result: The 2-Local Stoquastic Hamiltonian problem on a 2D square qubit lattice is StoqMA-complete.
conclusion: This establishes a fundamental complexity result for stoquastic Hamiltonians, with implications for quantum simulation and complexity theory.

title: Quantum Optimal Control For Coherent Spin Dynamics Of Radical Pairs Via Pontryagin Maximum Principle
authors: Ugur G. Abdulla, Jose H. Rodrigues, And Jean-Jacques Slotine
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2096 (2026).

This paper aims to devise the shape of the external electromagnetic field that drives the spin dynamics of radical pairs to a quantum coherent state through maximization of the triplet-born singlet yield in biochemical reactions. The model is a Schrödinger system with spin Hamiltonians given by the sum of Zeeman interaction and hyperfine coupling interaction terms. We introduce a one-parameter family of optimal control problems by coupling the Schrödinger system to a control field through filtering equations for the electromagnetic field. Fréchet differentiability and the Pontryagin Maximum Principle in Hilbert space are proved, and the bang-bang structure of the optimal control is established. A new iterative Pontryagin Maximum Principle (IPMP) method for the identification of the bang-bang optimal control is developed. Numerical simulations based on IPMP and the gradient projection method (GPM) in Hilbert spaces are pursued, and the convergence, stability, and the regularization effect are demonstrated. Comparative analysis of filtering with regular optimal electromagnetic field versus non-filtering with bang-bang optimal field ([MATH][MATH]) demonstrates that the change of the maxima of the singlet yield is less than 1%. The results open a venue for a potential experimental work on magnetoreception as a manifestation of quantum biological phenomena.

.
tldr: This paper uses optimal control theory to maximize singlet yield in radical pair spin dynamics, with potential applications to magnetoreception.
motivation: To understand how external electromagnetic fields can control quantum coherence in radical pairs, which is relevant to biochemical reactions and magnetoreception.
method: Formulates an optimal control problem for the Schrödinger equation with Zeeman and hyperfine interactions, proves Fréchet differentiability and Pontryagin Maximum Principle in Hilbert space, and develops an iterative PMP method for bang-bang control.
result: The optimal control is bang-bang; numerical simulations show that filtering with regular fields vs. bang-bang fields yields less than 1% difference in singlet yield maxima.
conclusion: The results suggest potential experimental work on magnetoreception as a quantum biological phenomenon, but the paper is primarily about control theory methodology.

title: Construction Of near-Γ Multiple Chiral Exceptional Points In Momentum Space Of Photonic Crystal Slabs
authors: Jingyu Zhang, Yang Gao, Tianfu Ma, Wenjia Li, Weimin Ye And Jianlong Liu
abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) in optical systems have attracted considerable attention because of their nontrivial topological properties and unusual physical effects. Among them, scattering EPs are particularly appealing for describing chiral response through the scattering matrix. Photonic crystal slabs offer a versatile platform for studying chiral scattering EPs in momentum space, where their topological evolution can be conveniently accessed and engineered. In this work, a convenient approach is presented for achieving chiral scattering EPs near the Γ point by exploiting the topological evolution properties in the momentum space of photonic crystal slabs. By varying the structural parameters of the photonic crystal slabs, multiple chiral EPs are identified near the Γ point, with their evolution and annihilation processes systematically analyzed. Furthermore, the pronounced transmission asymmetry observed near the EP enables polarization conversion from linear to circular, functioning as a quarter-wave plate. This approach provides a straightforward method for realizing and controlling chiral EPs in momentum space, thereby expanding the potential for practical applications in optical metadevices.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to create multiple chiral exceptional points near the Γ point in photonic crystal slabs by tuning structural parameters.
motivation: Exceptional points in optical systems have unique topological properties and potential applications, but achieving and controlling chiral scattering EPs in momentum space remains challenging.
method: The authors use photonic crystal slabs as a platform and vary structural parameters to engineer the topological evolution of chiral scattering EPs near the Γ point, analyzing their evolution and annihilation.
result: Multiple chiral EPs are identified near the Γ point, and the transmission asymmetry near the EP enables linear-to-circular polarization conversion, functioning as a quarter-wave plate.
conclusion: This approach provides a straightforward method for realizing and controlling chiral EPs in momentum space, expanding potential applications in optical metadevices.

title: Integrated Error-suppressed Pipeline For Quantum Optimization Of Nontrivial Binary Combinatorial Optimization Problems On Gate-model Hardware At The 156-qubit Scale
authors: Natasha Sachdeva, Gavin S Hartnett, Smarak Maity, Samuel Marsh, Yulun Wang, Adam Winick, Ryan Dougherty, Daniel Canuto, You Quan Chong, G Adam Cox, Michael Hush, Pranav S Mundada, Christopher D B Bentley, Michael J Biercuk And Yuval Baum
abstract: We introduce a novel hybrid quantum–classical variational optimization method for unconstrained binary combinatorial optimization problems on gate-model quantum computers, integrating a custom variational ansatz, staged feedback-based dual variational parameter update strategies, efficient parametric compilation, automated error suppression during hardware execution, and scalable O( ) classical post-processing to correct for bitflip errors. Without this integrated approach, we show that standard circuit execution at scale produces output indistinguishable from random sampling, establishing the necessity of each pipeline component. We benchmark the method on IBM superconducting quantum computers for several optimization problems drawn from NP-hard problem classes, where the optimization is conducted on hardware with no use of classical simulation or prior knowledge of the solution. For Max-Cut on random regular graphs with topologies not matched to device connectivity, the method achieves approximation ratios (AR) of 100% for unweighted 3-regular graphs up to 156 nodes, weighted regular graphs up to 80 nodes, and weighted 7-regular graphs up 50 nodes. Applied to higher-order binary optimization, the method finds the ground state energy of 127- and 156-qubit spin-glass models matched to device topology with linear, quadratic, and cubic interaction terms, achieving ARs of at least 99.5% across all instances tested. The method consistently outperforms a classical local solver across all problems. Where published results on identical problem instances are available, our method demonstrates competitive or superior performance. These results demonstrate that an appropriately engineered variational approach enables gate-model quantum computers to produce high-quality solutions for binary optimization problems drawn from NP-hard problem classes at the 156-qubit scale, where naïve implementations are insufficient for good performance.
tldr: This paper presents a hybrid quantum-classical variational optimization pipeline for binary combinatorial problems on gate-model quantum computers, achieving high approximation ratios on up to 156 qubits.
motivation: To demonstrate that gate-model quantum computers can solve NP-hard binary optimization problems at scale with an integrated error-suppressed pipeline, overcoming the limitations of naive circuit execution.
method: The method combines a custom variational ansatz, staged feedback-based dual variational parameter updates, efficient parametric compilation, automated error suppression, and scalable classical post-processing for bitflip error correction.
result: The pipeline achieves 100% approximation ratios for Max-Cut on unweighted 3-regular graphs up to 156 nodes and at least 99.5% for spin-glass models up to 156 qubits, outperforming classical local solvers.
conclusion: The results show that appropriately engineered variational approaches enable gate-model quantum computers to produce high-quality solutions for binary optimization problems at the 156-qubit scale, but the paper does not directly address the user's research interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, quantum communication, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Geometry-resolved Suppression Of Patch-potential Heating In Skeleton-electrode Ion Traps
authors: Chon-Teng Belmiro Chu, Hao-Chung Chen, Ting Hsu, Hsiang-Yu Lo, Ming-Shien Chang And Guin-Dar Lin
abstract: We present a quantitative, geometry-resolved framework to evaluate the effects of patch-potential noise in realistic three-dimensional Paul-trap structures. As a concrete application, we analyze a skeleton-electrode architecture and compare its performance against a conventional blade trap under identical ion-to-electrode distances and matched confinement parameters. The skeleton geometry achieves a suppression of motional heating exceeding 50%, with heating rate ratios of for the axial mode and for the radial mode. Patch-by-patch heating maps reveal that over 99% of the noise contribution originates from electrode surfaces within 500 m of the ion. We identify that axial heating follows a non-monotonic profile, with dominant ‘hotspots’ located at an intermediate distance of approximately 110 m. This behavior is driven by the vectorial directionality of the electric-field components, which provide the strongest axial coupling at these intermediate regions. Guided by these maps, we demonstrate a proof-of-principle electrode reconfiguration where segmented gaps are aligned with identified hotspots. This strategy successfully reduces axial heating even when the total electrode surface area increases, confirming that the spatial distribution of noise coupling—rather than total conductor area—is the primary driver of motional heating. These findings establish geometry-guided design as a practical route to suppress heating in trapped-ion platform, and the proposed skeleton architecture is compatible with advanced fabrication techniques, including metal additive manufacturing.
tldr: This paper presents a geometry-resolved framework to evaluate patch-potential heating in ion traps, demonstrating that skeleton-electrode designs can suppress motional heating by over 50% compared to conventional blade traps.
motivation: Motional heating from patch-potential noise is a major decoherence source in trapped-ion quantum computing. The authors aimed to develop a quantitative, geometry-resolved understanding to guide trap design for heating suppression.
method: They used numerical simulations to compute patch-potential noise and heating rates for realistic 3D Paul-trap structures, comparing a skeleton-electrode architecture with a conventional blade trap. They generated patch-by-patch heating maps and analyzed the spatial distribution of noise coupling.
result: The skeleton geometry achieved >50% suppression of motional heating. Over 99% of noise comes from electrode surfaces within 500 μm of the ion. Axial heating shows non-monotonic behavior with hotspots at ~110 μm. Reconfiguring electrode gaps to align with hotspots reduces heating even with increased total surface area.
conclusion: Geometry-guided design is a practical route to suppress heating in trapped-ion platforms. The skeleton architecture is compatible with advanced fabrication like metal additive manufacturing, offering a path to lower decoherence.

title: Probing A Theoretical Framework For A Photonic Extreme Learning Machine
authors: Vicente Rocha, Duarte Silva, Felipe C Moreira, Catarina S Monteiro, Tiago D Ferreira And Nuno A Silva
abstract: The development of computing paradigms alternative to von Neumann architectures has recently fueled significant progress in novel all-optical processing solutions. In this work, we investigate how the coherence properties can be exploited for computing by expanding information onto a higher-dimensional space in the photonic extreme learning machine framework. A theoretical framework is provided based on the transmission matrix formalism, mapping the input plane onto the output camera plane, resulting in the establishment of the connection with complex extreme learning machines and derivation of upper bounds for the hidden space dimensionality as well as the form of the activation functions. Experiments using free-space propagation through a diffusive medium, performed in low-dimensional input space regimes, validate the model and the proposed estimator for the dimensionality. Overall, the framework presented and the findings enclosed have the potential to foster further research in a multitude of directions, from the development of robust general-purpose all-optical hardware to a full-stack integration with optical sensing devices toward edge computing solutions.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for photonic extreme learning machines using transmission matrix formalism and validates it with free-space propagation experiments.
motivation: To explore alternative computing paradigms beyond von Neumann architectures by exploiting coherence properties of light for all-optical processing.
method: The authors use transmission matrix formalism to map input to output planes, derive upper bounds for hidden space dimensionality and activation functions, and validate with experiments using free-space propagation through a diffusive medium.
result: The model connects photonic extreme learning machines to complex extreme learning machines, provides dimensionality estimators, and experimental validation in low-dimensional input regimes.
conclusion: The framework can foster development of all-optical hardware and edge computing solutions, but the paper is not directly relevant to the user's research interests in quantum information thermodynamics, foundations, communication, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Emergent Hydrodynamics Of Chiral Active Fluids: Vortices, Bubbles And Odd Diffusion
authors: Umberto Marini Bettolo Marconi, Alessandro Petrini, Raphael Maire And Lorenzo Caprini
abstract: Starting from a microscopic multiparticle Langevin equation, we obtain a hydrodynamic description in terms of density and momentum fields for chiral active particles interacting via standard repulsive and nonlocal odd forces. These odd interactions are reciprocal but non-conservative: they are non-potential forces, as they act perpendicular to the vector joining any pair of particles. As a result, the torques that two particles exert on one another are non-reciprocal. The ensuing macroscopic continuum description consists of a continuity equation for the density and a generalized compressible Navier–Stokes equation for the fluid velocity. The latter includes a chirality-induced torque density term and an odd viscosity contribution. Our theory predicts the emergence of odd diffusivity, edge currents, and is consistent with an inhomogeneous phase—characterized by bubble-like structures—recently observed in simulations. Specifically, the theory exhibits a linear instability arising from the interplay between odd viscosity and torque density, and admits steady-state inhomogeneous solutions featuring bubbles and vortices, in qualitative agreement with numerical simulations. Our findings can be tested experimentally in systems of granular spinners or rotating microorganisms suspended in a fluid.
tldr: This paper derives a hydrodynamic theory for chiral active fluids with odd interactions, predicting odd diffusion, edge currents, and bubble-like phases.
motivation: To understand the collective behavior of chiral active particles (e.g., rotating microorganisms) where interactions are non-conservative and lead to novel emergent phenomena.
method: Starting from a microscopic multiparticle Langevin equation, the authors coarse-grain to obtain continuum equations for density and momentum, including odd viscosity and torque density terms.
result: The theory predicts odd diffusivity, edge currents, and a linear instability that leads to steady-state inhomogeneous solutions with bubbles and vortices, matching simulations.
conclusion: The findings provide a theoretical framework for chiral active fluids and can be tested in experiments with granular spinners or rotating microorganisms.

title: Probing Electron Correlations In Solids With Auger-photoelectron Coincidence Spectroscopy
authors: Roberto Gotter And Giovanni Stefani Robert A Bartynski
abstract: Auger photoelectron coincidence spectroscopy (APECS) has emerged as a powerful tool for probing electron–electron correlation in solids. When a photoexcited core hole decays via a core-valence-valence Auger transition, two valence holes are created in the final state. Consequently, the line shape of the Auger electron spectrum is influenced by both Coulomb and exchange interactions between the two holes. By simultaneously detecting the photoelectron and Auger electron emitted from a single photoionization event, APECS measurements place constraints on the two final state holes, enabling one to independently measure Coulomb and exchange correlation energies.
