[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064108] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage-time properties of diffusion with stochastic diffusion coefficients in one dimension.
motivation: To understand diffusion in heterogeneous environments or of particles with conformational fluctuations, where the diffusion coefficient itself fluctuates stochastically.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of first-passage-time statistics for a broad class of positive stochastic diffusion coefficients in one-dimensional diffusion.
result: The paper derives general properties of first-passage times, showing how stochasticity in the diffusion coefficient affects the distribution and moments of first-passage times.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into transport in disordered media and may inform models of stochastic processes in physics and biology.

title: Relative-advection-induced Instability In A Reaction-diffusion-advection System

The instability mechanism in general reaction-diffusion-advection systems is key to understanding flow-driven self-organization. Here we report the general conditions for instability in [MATH]-dimensional space, formally termed relative advection instability (RAI) given its exclusive dependence on the …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064202] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies instability in reaction-diffusion-advection systems, which is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand flow-driven self-organization in classical reaction-diffusion-advection systems.
method: Theoretical analysis of general conditions for instability in n-dimensional space, focusing on relative advection.
result: Identified a new instability mechanism called relative advection instability (RAI) that depends solely on advection differences.
conclusion: Provides general conditions for pattern formation in advective systems, with implications for ecology and fluid dynamics.

title: Resetting-induced Instability In Queues Fed By A Search Process In An Interval
authors: José Giral-Barajas And Paul C. Bressloff
abstract:
Author(s): José Giral-Barajas and Paul C. Bressloff

Proper management of resources whose arrival and consumption are subject to environmental randomness is an intrinsic process in both natural and artificial systems. This phenomenon can be modeled as a queuing process whose arrival distribution is determined by a search process with stochastic resett…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064101] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies instability in queues where arrivals are governed by a search process with stochastic resetting, a topic in statistical physics and queueing theory.
motivation: To understand how resetting events in a search process affect the stability of a queue, which has implications for resource management in natural and artificial systems.
method: The authors model the arrival process as a search with stochastic resetting in an interval and analyze the queue length distribution and stability conditions using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that resetting can induce instability in the queue, leading to diverging mean queue lengths under certain conditions, and characterize the phase transition between stable and unstable regimes.
conclusion: The work highlights the impact of resetting on queue dynamics and suggests future studies on more complex resetting protocols or service disciplines.

title: Quantum Size Effect And Two-step Condensation Of Ideal Bose Atoms In An Optical Hard-wall Nanotube
authors: Ze Cheng

We consider a quasi-one-dimensional (quasi-1D) system that is an optical hard-wall nanotube with axial harmonic potential. This quasi-1D system possesses a quasi-1D harmonic potential that consists of a 1D harmonic trap along the [MATH] axis and a two-dimensional box trap in the [MATH] plane. Wit…

tldr: This paper studies Bose-Einstein condensation in a quasi-1D optical nanotube with hard-wall and harmonic confinement, focusing on quantum size effects and two-step condensation.
motivation: To understand how quantum confinement in quasi-1D geometries affects Bose-Einstein condensation, particularly the role of hard-wall boundaries and harmonic traps.
method: Theoretical analysis using ideal Bose gas model in a quasi-1D harmonic potential with a 2D box trap, solving the grand canonical ensemble and computing condensation temperatures.
result: Predicts a two-step condensation process and quantum size effects due to the discrete energy levels in the transverse direction.
conclusion: Provides insights into low-dimensional Bose condensation, but the system is idealized and may not directly apply to experimental realizations.

title: Relaxation Of The Random Site Coulomb Glass Model In Two Dimensions
authors: Preeti Bhandari And Vikas Malik

Author(s): Preeti Bhandari and Vikas Malik

This study investigates the influence of material density, disorder in onsite energies, and localization length on relaxation dynamics within a two-dimensional random site Coulomb glass model at half-filling. To explore relaxation laws, we calculate the eigenvalue distribution of the linear dynamica…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064107] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies relaxation dynamics in a two-dimensional random site Coulomb glass model, focusing on the influence of disorder and localization length.
motivation: To understand how material density, disorder, and localization length affect relaxation in disordered electronic systems, which is relevant for glassy dynamics and transport.
method: Numerical calculation of eigenvalue distributions of the linear dynamics matrix for the random site Coulomb glass model at half-filling.
result: The relaxation laws depend on density, disorder strength, and localization length, with specific eigenvalue distributions characterizing the dynamics.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into relaxation in disordered systems, but the paper is not directly connected to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Competition Between Private And Expressed Opinions In Binary Choice: The $α\text{−}\mathrm{EPO}$ $q$-voter Model
authors: Barbara Kamińska, Barbara Nowak, Arkadiusz Lipiecki, And Katarzyna Sznajd-Weron
abstract:

People often express opinions that differ from their privately held views, a phenomenon known in economy as preference falsification. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 064301] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a sociophysics model of opinion dynamics where agents have both private and expressed opinions, focusing on the competition between them in binary choices.
motivation: To understand the phenomenon of preference falsification, where individuals publicly express opinions that differ from their private beliefs, using a statistical physics approach.
method: The authors introduce the α-EPO q-voter model, an extension of the q-voter model, where each agent has two binary variables (private and expressed opinion) and update rules based on social influence and conformity.
result: The model exhibits various phases including consensus, polarization, and a 'private opinion dominance' phase, depending on parameters like the fraction of conformists and the number of influencing neighbors.
conclusion: The work provides insights into how social pressure can lead to a gap between private and expressed opinions, with potential applications in understanding public opinion dynamics and social phenomena.

title: Learning Stochastic Cellular Dynamics From Snapshots Through Bidirectional Causal Neural Stochastic Differential Equations
authors: Yuting Meng, Rabia Sultan, Peixuan Jiang, Qiuman Wang, Dian Tan, Jiao Wang, Peiluan Li, And Luonan Chen
abstract:

Due to cell destruction in sequencing, time-series data yield unpaired snapshots, obscuring lineages and gene dynamics in individual cells. Current data-driven methods rely on single-variate expression, ignoring cell types and rotational effects in nonsteady states, limiting interpretability and acc…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064401] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a causal neural SDE framework to infer stochastic cellular dynamics from unpaired snapshot data, focusing on gene regulatory networks and cell differentiation.
motivation: Time-series single-cell sequencing destroys cells, yielding unpaired snapshots that obscure lineage and gene dynamics; existing methods ignore cell types and rotational effects in nonsteady states.
method: The authors propose a bidirectional causal neural stochastic differential equation (SDE) model that learns latent dynamics from snapshot data by incorporating causal structures and handling nonsteady-state rotational effects.
result: The model successfully reconstructs continuous cell trajectories and gene regulatory interactions from unpaired snapshots, outperforming existing methods on synthetic and real datasets.
conclusion: This work provides a powerful tool for inferring cellular dynamics from destructive measurements, with potential applications in developmental biology and disease modeling.

title: Intrinsic Noise Suppression In Protein Allostery: Quantifying Pathway Redundancy Via Spanning Tree Statistics
authors: Burak Erman

Author(s): Burak Erman

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064402] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a spanning-tree-based framework to quantify allosteric communication pathways and noise suppression in proteins, which is unrelated to the user's research interests.
motivation: To understand how multiple communication pathways in protein allostery contribute to signal transmission and noise suppression.
method: Spanning-tree-based statistical framework to analyze residue contact networks.
result: Quantified pathway redundancy and its role in intrinsic noise suppression.
conclusion: Provides insights into allosteric regulation but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Oscillatory Evolutionarily Stable State And Limit Cycle In Replicator Dynamics
authors: Suman Chakraborty, Vikash Kumar Dubey, Vaibhav Madhok, And Sagar Chakraborty

motivation: To extend the concept of evolutionarily stable states to non-equilibrium oscillatory behaviors in population dynamics.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of replicator dynamics models, focusing on conditions for oscillatory ESS and limit cycles.
result: Identified conditions under which oscillatory states can be evolutionarily stable, and characterized limit cycle attractors.
conclusion: Provides a framework for understanding cyclic evolutionary strategies, with potential applications in biology and social sciences.

authors: Leiming Chen, Chiu Fan Lee, And John Toner

Dry active matter in an anisotropic medium is of experimental relevance, and the interplay between anisotropy and the dynamics of the active matter remains under-explored. title: Wave Breaking And Electron Heating Of Perpendicularly Propagating $x$-mode Waves In Magnetized Plasmas
authors: Jin-Ze Liu, Heng Zhang, Dong-Ning Gao, And Wen-Shan Duan

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 055423] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective dynamics of macroscopic photoactive particles under alternating light patterns, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how spatiotemporal excitation patterns affect the collective motion of active particles.
method: Experiments with photoactive self-propelled particles in an arena with alternating bright and dark regions.
result: The particles exhibit collective dynamics influenced by the alternating excitation patterns.
conclusion: The findings contribute to active matter physics but are unrelated to the user's research interests.

We present a comprehensive discussion of a transition from integrability to nonintegrability in an oval billiard with a static boundary. This transition is controlled by a deformation parameter [MATH], which modifies the boundary shape from circular, corresponding to [MATH] and an integrable dynamics, t…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 054220] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the transition from integrability to nonintegrability in an oval billiard system, focusing on universal critical behavior in order-to-chaos transitions.
motivation: To understand the universal aspects of the transition from integrable to chaotic dynamics in Hamiltonian systems, using a billiard model with a tunable deformation parameter.
method: Numerical simulations and analytical scaling analysis of an oval billiard with a static boundary, varying a deformation parameter to control the transition.
result: Identified universal critical exponents and scaling laws characterizing the transition from order to chaos.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the universality of chaos transitions in classical Hamiltonian systems, with potential extensions to other nonlinear systems.

title: Emergent Domain Segregation In Self-interacting Polymers Explains Chromosome 3d Conformations In Single Human Cells
authors: Mattia Conte, Simona Bianco, Sougata Guha, Andrea M. Chiariello, Andrea Esposito, Alex Abraham, Sumanta Kundu, Francesca Vercellone, Andrea Fontana, Florinda Di Pierno, Ciro Di Carluccio, Matteo Olimpo, And Mario Nicodemi
abstract:

Polymer physics models have been employed to elucidate the 3D organization of chromosomes in the cell nucleus. However, how well they capture chromatin architectures at the single-molecule level remains poorly understood. Here, we consider a minimal polymer model where folding is driven by sequence-…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 054416] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a minimal polymer model to study chromosome 3D organization in single cells, focusing on domain segregation driven by self-interactions.
motivation: To understand how well polymer physics models capture chromatin architecture at the single-molecule level, which is poorly understood.
method: A minimal polymer model with sequence-dependent interactions is used to simulate chromosome folding and compare with single-cell Hi-C data.
result: The model reproduces emergent domain segregation and key features of chromosome 3D conformations observed in single human cells.
conclusion: The findings validate the polymer model for single-cell chromatin organization and suggest that simple physical principles can explain complex genome architecture.

title: Time Delay In The One-dimensional Swarmalator Model
authors: K. P. O'keeffe, Rommel Tchinda Djeudjo, And Jason Hindes
abstract:
Author(s): K. P. O'Keeffe, Rommel Tchinda Djeudjo, and Jason Hindes

We study the one-dimensional (1D) swarmalator model with time-delayed interactions. Delay preserves the familiar static states—sync, async, and phase wave—but generates two new families of nonstatic states. One bifurcates from the phase wave at [MATH]; the other bifurcates from the async s…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 054219] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies time-delayed interactions in the 1D swarmalator model, revealing new nonstatic states.
motivation: To understand how time delay affects collective behavior in swarmalator systems, which model swarming and synchronization.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of the 1D swarmalator model with time-delayed coupling.
result: Time delay preserves static states but introduces two new families of nonstatic states bifurcating from phase wave and async states.
conclusion: Time delay enriches the dynamics of swarmalator models, with implications for biological and robotic swarms.

title: Phenomenology Of Orbital Torque, Pumping, And Mixing Conductance In Metallic Bilayers
authors: Xiaobai Ning, Henri Jaffrès, Weisheng Zhao, And Aurélien Manchon
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaobai Ning, Henri Jaffrès, Weisheng Zhao, and Aurélien Manchon

The conversion between spin and orbital currents is at the origin of the orbital torque and its Onsager reciprocal, the orbital pumping. Here, we propose a phenomenological model to describe the orbital torque in magnetic bilayers composed of an orbital source (i.e., a light metal such as Ti, Ru, ${…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023239] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a phenomenological model for orbital torque and pumping in metallic bilayers, focusing on spin-orbit conversion in light metals.
motivation: To understand the conversion between spin and orbital currents in magnetic bilayers, which is key for orbital torque and its reciprocal effect.
method: A phenomenological model is proposed to describe orbital torque in bilayers composed of an orbital source (light metal) and a ferromagnet.
result: The model captures the orbital torque and pumping, and defines mixing conductance for orbital currents.
conclusion: Provides a framework for interpreting experiments on orbital torque and may guide future spintronic devices.

title: From Knots To Crystals: Machine-learned Potentials For Self-assembling Topological Solitons In Liquid Crystals
authors: Arunkumar Bupathy, Darian Hall, Ivan I. Smalyukh, Gerardo Campos-Villalobos, Rodolfo Subert, And Marjolein Dijkstra
abstract:

Knotted fields in classical and quantum systems have long been recognized for their nontrivial topologies and particlelike behavior, but practical applications have been limited by the difficulty of stabilizing them. Recently, stable knotted solitonic textures—heliknotons—were discovered in chiral l…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023235] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to develop interparticle potentials for self-assembling topological solitons (heliknotons) in liquid crystals.
motivation: To enable practical applications of knotted solitonic textures by stabilizing them and controlling their self-assembly into ordered structures.
method: Machine-learned potentials are derived from molecular simulations to model interactions between heliknotons, enabling large-scale simulations of their self-assembly.
result: The machine-learned potentials accurately reproduce the behavior of heliknotons and predict the formation of crystalline and other ordered phases.
conclusion: This approach provides a pathway to design materials with tailored topological properties, but the focus is on soft matter and liquid crystals, not quantum systems.

title: Brain-inspired, Interpretable, Resonant Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Mark A. Kramer
abstract:
Author(s): Mark A. Kramer

Traditional artificial neural networks consist of nodes with nonoscillatory dynamics. Biological neural networks, on the other hand, consist of oscillatory components embedded in an oscillatory environment. Motivated by this feature of biological neurons, we describe a neural network framework with …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023237] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a brain-inspired recurrent neural network with oscillatory nodes, but it is not directly related to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Biological neural networks exhibit oscillatory dynamics, unlike traditional artificial neural networks with nonoscillatory nodes. The author aims to create a more biologically plausible neural network framework.
method: The paper describes a neural network framework where nodes have oscillatory dynamics, inspired by biological neurons. The approach likely involves differential equations or recurrent connections that produce resonant behavior.
result: The key findings are not detailed in the abstract, but the framework is claimed to be interpretable and resonant, potentially offering advantages for certain tasks.
conclusion: The implications are for machine learning and neuroscience, not for quantum computing or thermodynamics. Future directions may include applications in time-series analysis or cognitive modeling.

title: Large Deviations In non-Markovian Stochastic Epidemics
authors: Matan Shmunik And Michael Assaf
abstract:
Author(s): Matan Shmunik and Michael Assaf

Researchers study non-Markovian epidemic models in a well-mixed setting and reveal that the nonexponential waiting-time distributions between successive infection (and/or recovery) events can significantly alter the final outbreak-size distribution and disease lifetime compared with the Markovian case.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022038] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies large deviations in non-Markovian stochastic epidemic models, focusing on how nonexponential waiting-time distributions affect outbreak size and disease lifetime.
motivation: To understand the impact of non-Markovian effects on epidemic dynamics, which are often neglected in standard Markovian models.
method: Analytical and numerical methods for large deviation theory applied to stochastic epidemic models with nonexponential waiting-time distributions.
result: Non-Markovian waiting-time distributions significantly alter the final outbreak-size distribution and disease lifetime compared to Markovian cases.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of considering non-Markovian effects in epidemic modeling, with implications for predicting and controlling outbreaks.

title: Shaping Boundaries To Control And Transport Topological Defects In Colloidal Nematic Liquid Crystals

Anisotropic rodlike particles form liquid crystalline phases with varying degrees of orientational and translational order. When confined geometrically, these phases can give rise to topological defects, which can be selected and controlled by tuning how the rods align near boundaries, known as anch…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023217] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how geometric confinement and boundary anchoring control topological defects in colloidal nematic liquid crystals.
motivation: To understand and control topological defects in liquid crystals for potential applications in materials science and soft matter.
method: Experimental and computational study of colloidal nematic liquid crystals confined by shaped boundaries with controlled anchoring conditions.
result: Boundary shape and anchoring can select and manipulate the type and location of topological defects.
conclusion: Provides insights for designing liquid crystal devices that exploit topological defects.

title: Quantum Optical Electron Pulse Shaper
authors: Neli Laštovičková Streshkova And Martin Kozák
abstract:
Author(s): Neli Laštovičková Streshkova and Martin Kozák

Coherent control of ultrafast quantum phenomena benefits from pulse-shaping capabilities allowing to modulate the envelope and instantaneous phase of optical fields on femtosecond timescales. While such control is available for optical fields, an analogy of a pulse shaper for freely propagating elec…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023222] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a quantum optical electron pulse shaper for coherent control of free electrons, which is not directly related to the user's research interests.
motivation: To extend pulse-shaping capabilities from optical fields to freely propagating electrons, enabling coherent control of ultrafast quantum phenomena.
method: The authors likely use optical modulation techniques adapted for electron beams, possibly involving laser-induced near-fields or photonic structures.
result: Demonstration of a device that can shape the envelope and phase of electron pulses on femtosecond timescales.
conclusion: This work opens new possibilities for coherent control of electron beams, with potential applications in ultrafast electron microscopy and quantum optics.

title: Compositional Disorder In A Multicomponent Nonreciprocal Mixture: Stability And Patterns
authors: Laya Parkavousi And Suropriya Saha
abstract:
Author(s): Laya Parkavousi and Suropriya Saha

In passive phase-separating mixtures, the average density of each component can be tuned to control the composition of the coexisting bulk phases. This concept extends to active systems. For example, in a nonreciprocal mixture of two species, changing the average density of either species alters the…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023223] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies compositional disorder and pattern formation in a multicomponent nonreciprocal mixture, focusing on stability and pattern dynamics.
motivation: To understand how average densities of components affect phase behavior in nonreciprocal active mixtures, extending concepts from passive phase separation.
method: Theoretical analysis using linear stability analysis and numerical simulations of a multicomponent mixture with nonreciprocal interactions.
result: Changing average densities alters the composition of coexisting phases and can lead to various pattern formations, including traveling waves and static patterns.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into controlling phase behavior in active mixtures, with potential applications in biological and synthetic active systems.

title: Online Learning Of Eddy-viscosity And Backscattering Closures For Geophysical Turbulence Using Ensemble Kalman Inversion
authors: Yifei Guan, Pedram Hassanzadeh, Tapio Schneider, Oliver Dunbar, Daniel Zhengyu Huang, Jinlong Wu, And Ignacio Lopez-Gomez
abstract:
Author(s): Yifei Guan, Pedram Hassanzadeh, Tapio Schneider, Oliver Dunbar, Daniel Zhengyu Huang, Jinlong Wu, and Ignacio Lopez-Gomez

This work combines ensemble Kalman inversion with calibration, emulation, and sampling to estimate closure parameters and their uncertainties for large-eddy simulations of two-dimensional geophysical turbulence. Across several flow regimes, the optimized parameters remain nearly constant and agree with semianalytical predictions.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023215] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses ensemble Kalman inversion to learn closure parameters for large-eddy simulations of geophysical turbulence, with no connection to quantum information or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To improve large-eddy simulations of geophysical turbulence by learning eddy-viscosity and backscattering closures from data.
method: Combines ensemble Kalman inversion with calibration, emulation, and sampling to estimate closure parameters and their uncertainties.
result: Optimized parameters remain nearly constant across flow regimes and agree with semianalytical predictions.
conclusion: The approach provides a robust way to parameterize unresolved turbulence in geophysical flows, but has no relevance to quantum computing or information thermodynamics.

title: Reynolds Number Effect On Dynamical State In A Fully Developed Turbulent Channel Flow
authors: Yusuke Nabae, Hiroya Mamori, And Hiroshi Gotoda

We investigate the Reynolds number effect on the dynamical state of a turbulent channel flow by means of orbital-instability-based forecasting method (OIFM) and ordinal partition transition network (OPTN). In the near-wall region, i.e., viscous sublayer and buffer layer, the coexistence of streaky s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023205] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of Reynolds number on dynamical states in turbulent channel flow using orbital-instability-based forecasting and ordinal partition transition networks.
motivation: To understand how Reynolds number influences the dynamical state of turbulence in channel flow, which is important for fluid dynamics but not directly related to the user's interests.
method: Orbital-instability-based forecasting method (OIFM) and ordinal partition transition network (OPTN) are applied to analyze turbulent channel flow data.
result: The study finds that in the near-wall region, the coexistence of streaky structures is affected by Reynolds number, indicating changes in dynamical state.
conclusion: The findings contribute to understanding turbulence dynamics but have no direct implications for quantum information, thermodynamics, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein
abstract:
Author(s): Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, and Mahmoud I. Hussein

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021045] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces 'super-resonance' to overcome the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, with an application to flow control.
motivation: To break the inherent bandwidth limitation of conventional resonance, enabling broadband out-of-phase response for applications like flow stabilization.
method: The authors propose a theoretical framework for super-resonance, likely involving coupled resonators or metamaterials, and demonstrate its effect on flow control.
result: Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization.
conclusion: The concept of super-resonance could have broad implications for wave-based devices and flow control, but its relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is not evident.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature, characterized by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: To find and characterize flat-band materials that can host strongly correlated electron states at room temperature, which are typically only observed at low temperatures.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to measure the electronic band structure of layered transition-metal oxyhalides.
result: Intrinsic flat bands that are orbital-selective and remain stable at room temperature were observed.
conclusion: These materials provide a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron physics at room temperature, potentially enabling new quantum phenomena and applications.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, revealing hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment.
motivation: To understand and mitigate thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors by characterizing the mechanical properties of silica thin films.
method: Experimental characterization of elastic and structural properties of silica films using techniques such as Brillouin light scattering and X-ray diffraction.
result: Silica films exhibit hidden anisotropy that is not removed by standard heat treatment, affecting their elastic behavior.
conclusion: The findings inform coating design and deposition strategies to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles, revealing suppressed density fluctuations yet enhanced susceptibility at the liquid-vapor critical point.
motivation: To understand how hyperuniformity, a state with suppressed long-wavelength density fluctuations, affects liquid-gas critical phenomena, which is a fundamental question in statistical physics.
method: The authors likely use theoretical modeling and possibly simulations of spinning particle systems to analyze the equation of state and critical exponents near the liquid-vapor critical point.
result: Hyperuniform fluids exhibit unusual calmness (suppressed fluctuations) but high susceptibility at the critical point, challenging typical critical opalescence behavior.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new class of critical behavior in hyperuniform systems, with implications for designing materials with tailored fluctuation properties.

title: Intertwined Polar, Chiral, And Ferro-Rotational Orders In A Homo-Ferro-Rotational Insulator

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of a uniform ferro-rotational state in NiI2 that couples polarity and chirality, leading to complex domain walls.
motivation: To explore the interplay between polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a single material.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques were used to study NiI2.
result: A uniform ferro-rotational state was identified that couples polarity and chirality, forming complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The findings reveal new types of domain walls and may inform future studies of multiferroic materials.

title: Tracking Ultrafast Ion Diffusion Dynamics In ${\mathrm{AgCrSe}}_{2}$ Superionic Conductor
authors: Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, And Jiaqing He
abstract:
Author(s): Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, and Jiaqing He

Direct spatial and temporal characterization of ion diffusion in superionic conductors provides a better link to macroscopic properties and high-performance material design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021024] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses ultrafast electron diffraction to directly track ion diffusion dynamics in the superionic conductor AgCrSe2.
motivation: To directly observe and characterize ion diffusion in superionic conductors at ultrafast timescales, linking microscopic dynamics to macroscopic properties.
method: Ultrafast electron diffraction with pump-probe techniques to capture time-resolved structural changes.
result: Direct spatial and temporal mapping of ion diffusion pathways and rates in AgCrSe2.
conclusion: Provides insights for designing high-performance superionic conductors, but no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of a dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, which is a condensed matter physics result with no direct connection to the user's research interests.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex ordering phenomena; understanding the nematic state is key to their behavior.
method: The study likely uses experimental techniques (e.g., neutron scattering, dielectric spectroscopy) and theoretical modeling to characterize the dipolar nematic phase.
result: A dipolar nematic state is identified as the underlying order in relaxor ferroelectrics.
conclusion: This finding advances the fundamental understanding of relaxor ferroelectrics but has no immediate implications for information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, quantum communication, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Effect Of Glass Stability On The Low Frequency Vibrations Of Vapor Deposited Glasses
authors: I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, And G. Baldi
abstract:
Author(s): I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, and G. Baldi

An improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique helps clarify the connections between complex vibrations and the properties of glasses.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021021] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-frequency vibrations in vapor-deposited glasses and their relation to glass stability using inelastic x-ray scattering.
motivation: To clarify the connection between complex vibrational properties and the stability of glasses, which is a fundamental question in condensed matter physics.
method: Improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique to measure low-frequency vibrational spectra of vapor-deposited glasses with varying stability.
result: The low-frequency vibrations are correlated with the degree of glass stability, providing insights into the boson peak and other vibrational anomalies.
conclusion: The findings help understand the microscopic origin of glass stability and may guide the design of ultrastable glasses.

title: Excitations Across The Equilibrium And Photoinduced “Hidden” States Of Magnetoresistive Manganites
authors: Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, And Jonathan Pelliciari
abstract:
Author(s): Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, and Jonathan Pelliciari

Ultrafast photoexcitation in /3Ca1/3MnO3 generates a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations that do not exist under standard equilibrium conditions.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021018] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced hidden phases in magnetoresistive manganites, focusing on polaronic and phononic excitations.
motivation: To understand the nonequilibrium dynamics and hidden phases in strongly correlated electron systems, specifically manganites.
method: Ultrafast photoexcitation and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) to probe excitations.
result: A long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations not present in equilibrium was observed.
conclusion: The findings reveal new pathways for controlling material properties via light, with potential implications for ultrafast devices.

title: More Is Less In Unpercolated Active Solids
authors: Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, And Anton Souslov
abstract:
Author(s): Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, and Anton Souslov

By combining experiments with robotic metamaterials and theory, this work shows that increasing microscopic activity can counterintuitively cause a solid’s macroscale active response to vanish when active units are too sparse for the active forces to percolate through the structure.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021012] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: Increasing microscopic activity in unpercolated active solids can counterintuitively cause the macroscopic active response to vanish.
motivation: To understand how the density of active units affects the collective mechanical response in active solids, particularly when active forces are too sparse to percolate.
method: Combined experiments with robotic metamaterials and theoretical modeling to study the effect of activity on macroscopic response.
result: When active units are sparse, increasing activity leads to a decrease in the overall active response, a 'more is less' effect.
conclusion: The percolation of active forces is crucial for maintaining macroscopic activity; this work provides insights into designing active metamaterials.

title: Boosting The Thermoelectric Performance Of $α$-MgAgSb Through Phase-Transition-Induced Self-Doping
authors: Kaiwei Guo, Tianyu Wang, Zhen Fan, Lunhua He, Fuhong Chen, Yi Wang, Qi Zhao, Jiawei Yang, Hangtian Zhu, Jun Li, Te-Huan Liu, And Huaizhou Zhao
abstract:

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the history and scientific legacy of the Arecibo 305-m radio telescope, highlighting its contributions to pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
motivation: To provide a historical perspective on Arecibo's impact on radio astronomy and atmospheric science, emphasizing how upgrades expanded its capabilities.
method: Historical review and synthesis of Arecibo's major scientific contributions across multiple subfields.
result: Arecibo enabled breakthroughs in pulsar timing, neutral hydrogen mapping, VLBI imaging, SETI, and the first detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.
conclusion: The telescope's legacy endures through its data and the scientific community it fostered, but the paper does not address the user's specific research interests.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the prospects for multimessenger astronomy combining continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars with electromagnetic observations, focusing on future detectors.
motivation: To assess the detection potential of continuous gravitational waves and their astrophysical implications, especially in dense neutron star environments.
method: Review of theoretical and observational status, including detector capabilities and multimessenger synergies.
result: Future detectors will improve sensitivity, but detection remains challenging; simultaneous electromagnetic observations are crucial.
conclusion: Multimessenger observations could reveal new physics in extreme matter, but the paper does not directly address the user's specific interests in quantum information or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection in ground-based interferometers.
motivation: To summarize progress in modeling core collapse supernovae and predicting gravitational wave signals for multimessenger astronomy.
method: Review of recent core collapse supernova models and gravitational wave signal predictions, along with detection methods for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: The paper presents the latest modeling advances and signal predictions, but no new results are reported.
conclusion: The review highlights the potential for multimessenger observations of a Galactic supernova, but does not directly address the user's research interests.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses how gravitational-wave and X-ray observations of neutron stars constrain the dense matter equation of state.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities, which is not accessible in terrestrial experiments.
method: Review of observational data from binary neutron star mergers (gravitational waves) and X-ray pulse profile measurements, compared to nuclear theory predictions.
result: New constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities have been obtained, improving our understanding of the nuclear equation of state.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine the equation of state and may reveal exotic matter phases.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a tension between the dipole in the cosmic microwave background and that in large-scale structure catalogs, which challenges the cosmological principle and the ΛCDM model.
motivation: To test the cosmological principle, a foundational assumption of the standard ΛCDM model, by comparing the dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the CMB.
method: Analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to measure the dipole in the matter distribution and compare it with the CMB dipole, including assessments of biases and systematic effects.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the matter dipole and the CMB dipole, suggesting a violation of the cosmological principle.
conclusion: The anomaly may challenge the standard ΛCDM model, and further investigation is needed to rule out systematic errors or explore alternative cosmological models.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: This review covers atomic-scale microscopy techniques for measuring disorder in semiconductors, with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how atomic-scale disorder affects semiconductor properties, which is important for materials science but not for the user's research interests.
method: Review of three real-space techniques: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, applied to compound semiconductors.
result: The techniques provide direct access to atomic-scale disorder, and combining them yields a more complete picture of defects.
conclusion: The paper is a materials science review with no implications for quantum computing, thermodynamics, or quantum communication.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the quantum-mechanical theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and experimental approaches to study them.
motivation: Nuclear reactions in stars occur at very low energies with small rates, making direct measurement difficult; a theoretical understanding is needed for stellar burning and element formation.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks including tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses new experimental ideas.
result: The review presents the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reaction theory and highlights quantum phenomena governing stellar reactions.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive overview and suggests future directions for both theory and experiment in nuclear astrophysics.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: This review explores self-alignment in polar active matter, where particles align their orientation with their velocity, leading to novel collective behaviors.
motivation: To understand how self-alignment, as opposed to neighbor imitation, shapes motion in active systems and to unify existing models.
method: The paper provides a conceptual and mathematical framework, reviews existing models, and discusses experimental realizations.
result: Self-alignment enables single-particle orbiting in traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies, fundamentally altering collective dynamics.
conclusion: The framework opens avenues for designing smart materials and robotic swarms, but direct connections to quantum information or thermodynamics are absent.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique using laser-induced ultrasound, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To provide an overview of optoacoustic imaging principles, applications, and recent multimodal developments for biological and clinical research.
method: Review article summarizing the physics of optoacoustic signal generation, detection methods, and integration with optical microscopy.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy enables high-resolution imaging at depths of millimeters to centimeters using optical contrast.
conclusion: The method is promising for noninvasive biological imaging, but the paper does not address quantum or thermodynamic aspects.

authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.

motivation: To provide a modern treatment of the Biot instability and understand the formation of creases and cusps in soft materials.

result: Presents a comprehensive review of nonlinear elasticity approaches to buckling phenomena in soft matter.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses gravitational wave signals from the early universe, focusing on phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: To explore how gravitational waves can probe the first second of the universe, which is opaque to electromagnetic radiation.
method: Review of theoretical models and detection strategies for stochastic gravitational waves from cosmological sources.
result: Identifies potential signals from phase transitions, topological defects, and other early-universe phenomena.
conclusion: Gravitational waves offer a unique window into the early universe, with future detectors potentially revealing new physics.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: This review describes the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations, focusing on electronic structure methods and their applications.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the Wannier-function ecosystem, which is widely used in condensed-matter physics for electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper reviews various software tools and methods that implement Wannier functions, discussing their interoperability and applications.
result: The ecosystem includes tools for ultra-accurate integrations, topological invariants, and other materials properties.
conclusion: The Wannier-function ecosystem is a major instrument for electronic-structure community, enabling understanding and design of materials.

title: Kinetic Solitary Electrostatic Structures In Collisionless Plasma: Phase-space Holes
authors: I. H. Hutchinson
abstract:
Author(s): I. H. Hutchinson

Plasma is usually taught to be a quasineutral gas of charged and neutral particles that exhibits collective behavior. However, satellites regularly observe solitary potential structures in space plasmas that are isolated positive or negative potential humps, called electron or ion holes. In the 1970s, laboratory observations were made of electron holes. This review presents an overview of the observation of these electrostatic structures and presents their origin and their stability, using analytic theory and simulations. The role of kinetically unstable velocity distributions is identified as a key driver.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045007] Published Tue Dec 10, 2024.
tldr: This paper reviews kinetic solitary electrostatic structures (electron and ion holes) in collisionless plasma, focusing on their observation, origin, and stability.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of phase-space holes in plasma, which are commonly observed in space plasmas but not fully understood.
method: Analytic theory and simulations are used to study the formation and stability of these structures, driven by kinetically unstable velocity distributions.
result: Electron and ion holes are isolated potential humps that arise from kinetic instabilities; their properties and stability are characterized.
conclusion: The review consolidates understanding of these structures and identifies key drivers, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Evolutionary Vaccination Dynamics Under Higher-order Reinforcement Pressure
authors: Yikang Lu, Ying Wang, Alfonso de Miguel-Arribas, Lei Shi And Yamir Moreno
abstract: Vaccination games in higher-order settings remain underexplored, despite their importance in shaping opinions and collective decisions. Here, we introduce a parsimonious behavioral-epidemiological model to evaluate how peer reinforcement influences vaccination uptake. The framework consists of a two-layer multiplex: an epidemic layer governed by the susceptible-infected-recovered process on a square lattice, and a behavioral layer represented by a hypergraph of triadic interactions. Individuals update their vaccination strategy via imitation, modulated by a reinforcement modulation parameter when local agreement with a like-minded peer is present. We find that higher-order structure alone induces clusters of vaccinated individuals that act as protective barriers. Small but nonzero values of ( ) maximize vaccination coverage and suppress outbreaks, while both the limiting case and larger values ( ) reduce uptake. This non-monotonic effect suggests that excessively strong local inhibition suppresses adaptability, whereas weaker inhibition facilitates the re-emergence of non-vaccinators. Our work bridges complex contagion theory with evolutionary game dynamics, offering insights into how contact structure and peer reinforcement jointly shape vaccination behavior.
tldr: This paper studies vaccination behavior using evolutionary game theory on hypergraphs, focusing on higher-order peer reinforcement effects.
motivation: To understand how higher-order social interactions (triadic) influence vaccination uptake, which is underexplored in vaccination games.
method: A two-layer multiplex model with an epidemic layer (SIR on lattice) and a behavioral layer (hypergraph of triadic interactions); individuals update strategies via imitation with a reinforcement modulation parameter.
result: Higher-order structure induces protective clusters; small reinforcement maximizes coverage, while zero or large reinforcement reduces uptake, showing a non-monotonic effect.
conclusion: The work bridges complex contagion and evolutionary game dynamics, offering insights for public health policy, but is not directly relevant to the user's research interests.

title: Electric-field-driven Nanoconfinement And The 5–120 Nm Stability Regime Of Piezoelectric Β-glycine
authors: Kexin Zhang And Zhengbao Yang
abstract: Piezoelectric β-glycine is a promising molecular crystal, yet its controlled preparation remains challenging. Current nanoconfinement strategies, which rely primarily on rigid templates or simulations, cannot reliably capture the intrinsic confinement regime that leads to β-phase formation. Here, we propose electric-field-driven nanoconfinement as a one-step, continuous, and interface-free approach to investigate glycine crystallization and to define the confinement regime that yields the β-phase. We produced glycine nanoparticles via electrohydrodynamic spraying under a direct current field, automatically varying the spraying height to modulate nanoconfinement during nucleation and growth. Structural, morphological, and piezoelectric characterizations reveal that pure β-glycine forms within a crystal radius range of 5–120 nm. By integrating these findings with thermodynamic and kinetic analysis, we elucidate the mechanism of β-phase formation and construct a crystallization phase map that delineates the confinement conditions necessary for its stabilization. This work identifies the critical nanoconfinement parameters for accessing piezoelectric β-glycine and provides fundamental insights into polymorph control in molecular crystalline materials.
tldr: This paper investigates electric-field-driven nanoconfinement to stabilize piezoelectric β-glycine nanocrystals within a 5–120 nm size range.
motivation: Controlled preparation of piezoelectric β-glycine is challenging; existing nanoconfinement methods cannot reliably capture the intrinsic confinement regime for β-phase formation.
method: Electrohydrodynamic spraying under a direct current field was used to produce glycine nanoparticles, with automatic variation of spraying height to modulate nanoconfinement during nucleation and growth.
result: Pure β-glycine forms within a crystal radius range of 5–120 nm; a crystallization phase map delineating confinement conditions for β-phase stabilization was constructed.
conclusion: This work identifies critical nanoconfinement parameters for accessing piezoelectric β-glycine and provides insights into polymorph control in molecular crystals.

title: Navigating High-order Protein Fitness Landscapes Via Deep Learning On Directed Evolution Trajectories
authors: Chengzhi Songliang Malingfeng Xueyingfan Xuqihan Zhangyuxi Liuchen Songyihan Linacenter For Quantitative Biology And Peking-Tsinghua Center For Life Sciences, Academy For Advanced Interdisciplinary Studies, Peking University, Beijing 100871, Chinabthe Ministry Of Education Key Laboratory Of Cell Proliferation And Differentiation, School Of Life Sciences, Peking University, Beijing 100871, Chinacpeking University Chengdu Academy For Advanced Interdisciplinary Biotechnologies, Chengdu, Sichuan 610213, China
abstract:
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 22, June 2026.
SignificanceMapping sequence–function landscape of target protein is fundamental to protein engineering and to a deeper understanding of protein function. While the effect of a single mutation is often studied, the impact of combining multiple mutations ...
tldr: This paper uses deep learning on directed evolution trajectories to map high-order protein fitness landscapes.
motivation: Understanding the impact of multiple mutations on protein function is crucial for protein engineering, but high-order epistasis is complex and poorly understood.
method: The authors apply deep learning models to sequence data from directed evolution experiments to predict fitness landscapes, capturing nonlinear interactions between mutations.
result: The deep learning approach accurately predicts high-order epistatic effects and identifies key mutations for improving protein fitness.
conclusion: This method can accelerate protein engineering by efficiently navigating combinatorial mutation spaces, with potential applications in biotechnology.
