title: Counting Votes With Multisets
authors: Bart Jacobs, Michael Johnson, Richard Buckland
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A multiset is a 'set' in which elements may occur multiple times. These structures are ideal for expressing the outcome of an election, for instance of the form 60 'yes' and 40 'no'. Moreover, multisets are a useful datatype in vote counting algorithms. This will be illustrated in three different forms of vote counting, known as: 'instant-runoff', 'De Borda', and 'single transferrable vote'. The relevant abstract properties of multisets are: (1) they form a (free) commutative monoid, and (2) they form a functor, and (3) also a monad. This paper illustrates how such categorical properties can be put to good use in deriving and expressing election outcomes. The emphasis is not on the (elementary) category theory involved, but on its application in voting systems.
tldr: This paper uses multisets and category theory to model and analyze voting algorithms, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To demonstrate the utility of multisets and categorical structures in vote counting algorithms.
method: The authors apply commutative monoids, functors, and monads to formalize instant-runoff, De Borda, and single transferable vote systems.
result: They show that categorical properties of multisets simplify the derivation and expression of election outcomes.
conclusion: The work highlights the value of abstract mathematical structures in practical voting systems, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: N-ary Quasi-arithmetic Means And Families Without Regularity
authors: Ekaterina Shulman Gergely Kiss
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical theorems of Kolmogorov--Nagumo--de Finetti and of Aczel--Maksa characterize quasi-arithmetic means from two complementary directions: the former for compatible families of means satisfying the replacement axiom, and the latter for bisymmetric means of fixed arity. We refine both representation results by showing that the required continuity follows automatically. Our main result states that every reflexive, symmetric, bisymmetric and partially strictly increasing [MATH]-variable operation on a real interval is continuous and hence quasi-arithmetic. The proof is based on a recursive construction on [MATH]-adic rationals given by bisymmetry, and a dense-domain continuity argument. The same method also yields the regularity-free Kolmogorov--Nagumo--de Finetti theorem for compatible families of strictly increasing symmetric means.
tldr: The paper proves that continuity in quasi-arithmetic mean characterizations follows from other axioms, eliminating the need for a separate regularity assumption.
motivation: Classical theorems require continuity as an explicit condition; the authors aim to show it is redundant under natural algebraic and monotonicity assumptions.
method: The proof uses a recursive construction on n-adic rationals via bisymmetry and a dense-domain continuity argument.
result: Every reflexive, symmetric, bisymmetric, and partially strictly increasing operation on a real interval is continuous and thus quasi-arithmetic; similarly for compatible families of means.
conclusion: The results refine classical representation theorems, showing that regularity is not an independent requirement, which may simplify future work in mean theory.

title: Some Properties Of Besov-Morrey Type Spaces
authors: A. Ussentay, K. Sadykova, N. Tleukhanova
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers Sobolev-Morrey and Besov-Morrey spaces. For Morrey spaces, multipliers are studied, and a theorem on multipliers from M_p^lambda(T) to M_p^lambda(T) is obtained for 1 < p < infinity and 0 <= lambda < 1/p. Based on this result, embeddings between Besov-Morrey and Sobolev-type spaces are established, namely B_1^alpha(M_p^lambda) embedded into W^alpha(M_p^lambda) embedded into B_infinity^alpha(M_p^lambda) for 0 < p <= infinity, 0 <= lambda <= 1/p, and alpha in R. In addition, an interpolation theorem for Besov-Morrey spaces is proved.
tldr: This paper studies embeddings and interpolation theorems for Besov-Morrey and Sobolev-Morrey function spaces, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To extend classical function space theory to Morrey-type spaces and establish multiplier and embedding results.
method: Analytical proofs using Fourier analysis, multiplier theory, and interpolation techniques.
result: Proved embeddings between Besov-Morrey and Sobolev-Morrey spaces, and an interpolation theorem for Besov-Morrey spaces.
conclusion: The results contribute to harmonic analysis and PDE theory, but have no direct application to the user's research interests.

title: On Parallel And Batch-Cutting Strategies For Norm-Minimization-Based Convex Vector Optimization
authors: Mohammed Alshahrani
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop parallel and batch-cutting variants of the norm-minimization-based outer approximation algorithm for convex vector optimization. The standard algorithm solves [MATH] independent subproblems at each iteration~[MATH] to evaluate all vertices of the current polyhedral approximation, but processes only the single best cut. We propose two improvements. First, we parallelize the across [MATH] workers, reducing per-iteration wall-clock time. Second, we introduce a batch-cutting strategy that adds up to [MATH] supporting halfspaces per iteration, using information from all solved subproblems rather than discarding it. We prove that the batch-cutting variant inherits the convergence rate [MATH] of the standard algorithm, where [MATH] is the number of outer iterations and [MATH] is the number of objectives. Computational experiments on eight test problems with [MATH] show that parallelism on 8 cores , and batch cutting consistently reduces the iteration count by 62--80\%. However, the wall-clock benefit of batch cutting is problem-dependent: the additional cuts per iteration accelerate vertex count growth, so batch cutting is most effective when per-vertex subproblem cost dominates.
tldr: This paper proposes parallel and batch-cutting strategies to accelerate a norm-minimization-based outer approximation algorithm for convex vector optimization.
motivation: To improve the computational efficiency of the standard algorithm, which solves many independent subproblems per iteration but only uses one cut.
method: Parallelizes subproblem solving across workers and introduces a batch-cutting strategy that adds multiple supporting halfspaces per iteration using information from all solved subproblems.
result: Parallelism on 8 cores and batch cutting reduce iteration count by 62-80%, but wall-clock benefit of batch cutting depends on per-vertex subproblem cost.
conclusion: The batch-cutting variant inherits the convergence rate of the standard algorithm and is most effective when subproblem cost dominates.

title: On Strong Identities Of Almost-canonically Seminormed Rings
authors: Jianqi Liu Xu Gao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the strong identity condition (SIC) for almost-canonically seminormed rings, a class of topological graded rings that includes enveloping algebras of vertex operator algebras. This condition was introduced in the algebro-geometric theory of conformal blocks, where it governs the smoothing of nodal curves. To understand the representation-theoretic meaning of SIC, we develop the representation theory of almost-canonically seminormed rings, including Zhu-type algebras, induced modules, rationality conditions, tensor product compatibility, and an end formula for the mode transition algebra. Our main result characterizes the strong identity condition in terms of orthogonal expansions, projectivity of canonical modules, and Morita-type equivalences induced by Zhu-type algebras. As an application, we show that for vertex operator algebras of CFT type, the smoothing property is equivalent to the Zhu algebra inducing a Morita-type equivalence with the category of admissible modules. Consequently, the strong identity condition identifies the precise representation-theoretic obstruction to extending algebraic smoothing beyond the semisimple setting. We further illustrate the theory through explicit examples, including the Weyl algebra and several irrational vertex operator algebras where the strong identity condition fails.
tldr: This paper studies strong identities in almost-canonically seminormed rings, a purely algebraic topic with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the representation-theoretic meaning of the strong identity condition (SIC) in the algebro-geometric theory of conformal blocks.
method: Develops representation theory of almost-canonically seminormed rings, including Zhu-type algebras, induced modules, and Morita-type equivalences.
result: Characterizes SIC in terms of orthogonal expansions and projectivity, and shows that for vertex operator algebras of CFT type, smoothing property is equivalent to a Morita-type equivalence.
conclusion: The strong identity condition identifies the obstruction to extending algebraic smoothing beyond the semisimple setting.

title: Shields: Automating Os Hardening With Iterative Multi-Agent Remediation
authors: Andrew Hamara, Dwight Horne, Aldehir Rojas, Timothy Kurniawan, Sophie Lamothe, Vishal Suresh, Nicholas Turoci, Lawrence Wong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Security misconfigurations remain a leading cause of OS-level compromise, and manually keeping systems compliant with standards like Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) is a tedious and expensive process. Existing compliance automation tools can reduce some of this burden, but they depend on static, pre-written corrective actions. In this paper, we introduce SHIELDS, a multi-agent system that uses large language models (LLMs) to approach OS hardening as an iterative, feedback-driven process. Instead of applying fixed remediations, SHIELDS continuously proposes fixes and refines them based on feedback from target system execution and validation scans. We evaluate the system across multiple virtual machine configurations using six contemporary LLMs ranging from 20B to 400B parameters, and find that SHIELDS successfully remediates up to 73% of scan findings. Our results also suggest that success in this setting depends less on model size (parameter count) than on effective tool use and information gathering, paving a practical path toward reducing the burden of security compliance in environments where compute is limited or security and privacy needs drive local model use.
tldr: SHIELDS is a multi-agent LLM system that automates OS hardening by iteratively proposing and refining fixes based on feedback from validation scans.
motivation: Manual OS hardening against security standards like DISA STIGs is tedious and expensive; existing automation tools rely on static, pre-written corrective actions.
method: The system uses multiple LLM agents to propose remediation steps, execute them on target VMs, and refine based on scan feedback, iterating until compliance is achieved.
result: SHIELDS remediated up to 73% of scan findings across various VM configurations using LLMs from 20B to 400B parameters; success depended more on tool use than model size.
conclusion: LLM-driven iterative remediation can reduce the burden of security compliance, especially in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive environments.

title: Dimensionality Reduction For Cyberattack Classification: A Comparative Evaluation Of Pca And Linear Predictive Coding
authors: Nelly Elsayed, Zag Elsayed, Navid Asadizanjani
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-dimensional feature representations are widely used in machine learning-based cyberattack detection systems. However, they increase computational complexity and may hinder deployment in resource-constrained environments. In this paper, we investigate feature compression techniques for cyberattack classification by comparing two dimensionality reduction approaches: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Linear Predictive Coding (LPC). Compressed feature representations with varying dimensionalities are generated and evaluated across several classification models. Experimental analysis demonstrates that PCA preserves classification performance even under aggressive compression. On the other hand, LPC provides competitive predictive representations with slightly larger performance degradation. The results show that substantial reductions in feature dimensionality can be achieved with minimal impact on classification accuracy, highlighting the potential of lightweight feature compression for efficient cybersecurity analytics.
tldr: This paper compares PCA and LPC for dimensionality reduction in cyberattack classification, showing that PCA preserves accuracy under aggressive compression.
motivation: High-dimensional features in cyberattack detection increase computational complexity, hindering deployment in resource-constrained environments.
method: The authors apply PCA and LPC to compress feature representations and evaluate classification performance across several models.
result: PCA maintains classification performance even with aggressive compression, while LPC shows slightly larger degradation.
conclusion: Substantial dimensionality reduction is possible with minimal accuracy loss, enabling lightweight cybersecurity analytics.

title: An Embarrassingly Simple Detector For Model Extraction Attacks In Large Language Model Api Traffic
authors: Shuze Liu, Qianwen Guo, Yushun Dong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed through hosted APIs, making model extraction a practical threat to model ownership and service security. However, individual extraction queries often resemble benign requests, and existing evaluations often focus on single-query anomaly scoring or pure benign-versus-attacker user settings. We formulate model extraction monitoring as benign-calibrated traffic-window distribution testing and show that an embarrassingly simple detector is effective: embed incoming queries into a semantic space and test whether their aggregate distribution deviates from historical benign traffic. We instantiate the detector with maximum mean discrepancy (MMD), using only benign-vs-benign comparisons to set the decision threshold. We evaluate on fourteen attacker-normal query pairs from four extraction scenarios and compare with adapted PRADA, SEAT, CAP, DATE, and marginal Mahalanobis baselines. Across three random seeds, MMD achieves 0.3% benign FPR, 100.0% pure-attacker TPR, 90.5% average TPR over attacker fractions, and 95.1% balanced accuracy. These results show that benign-calibrated distribution testing is a strong empirical baseline for model extraction detection in both user-level and mixed multi-user LLM API traffic. Code is released at: [URL].
tldr: This paper proposes a simple detector for model extraction attacks on LLM APIs using distribution testing with MMD.
motivation: Model extraction attacks threaten LLM service security, but existing detection methods are complex or focus on single queries.
method: The detector embeds queries into a semantic space and uses maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) to compare the distribution of incoming traffic against historical benign traffic, with thresholds set using benign-vs-benign comparisons.
result: The MMD detector achieves 0.3% benign FPR, 100% pure-attacker TPR, 90.5% average TPR over attacker fractions, and 95.1% balanced accuracy across 14 attack scenarios.
conclusion: Benign-calibrated distribution testing is a strong baseline for model extraction detection in LLM API traffic, with potential for further improvement.

title: SentinelRAG: Synthetic Sentinel Knowledge For Rag Database Copyright Protection
authors: Tsun On Kwok, Xi Yang, Ki Sen Hung, Chang Liu, Yangqiu Song
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Protecting proprietary RAG databases from unauthorized redistribution is challenging: existing watermarking methods either inject fabricated relations between real entities, polluting the knowledge base with misinformation, or embed fragile lexical patterns that adversarial paraphrasing easily removes. We propose SentinelRAG, a watermarking framework that embeds style-consistent but fictitious knowledge entries into the RAG database. Our key insight is that synthetic knowledge describing fictitious entities is unlikely to be retrieved by legitimate queries, yet can be reliably triggered through targeted probes known only to the data owner. Experiments on four datasets ranging from 2.9k to 8.8M documents demonstrate that SentinelRAG achieves statistically significant detection [MATH] across all tested configurations at only a 0.1% injection rate. Compared to the state-of-the-art, our method significantly reduces the false detection rate while maintaining negligible interference with legitimate user queries.
tldr: SentinelRAG embeds fictitious knowledge entries into RAG databases for copyright protection, with minimal impact on legitimate queries.
motivation: Protecting proprietary RAG databases from unauthorized redistribution without polluting the knowledge base or relying on fragile patterns.
method: Inject style-consistent but fictitious knowledge entries that are unlikely to be retrieved by legitimate queries but can be triggered by targeted probes.
result: Achieves statistically significant detection at only 0.1% injection rate across datasets, with lower false detection rate than state-of-the-art.
conclusion: Provides a robust watermarking method for RAG databases, but applicability to quantum or physics domains is not discussed.

title: GenTI: Benchmarking LLMs For Autonomous Idps Rule Generation For Unseen Attacks
authors: Hassan Jalil Hadi, Rehana Yasmin, Ali Shoker
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rule-based Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems (IDPS) offer precise attack detection as well as mitigation, however their manually crafted, signature-driven rules limit adaptability to emerging and zero-day threats. Additionally, existing public datasets (e.g., CICIDS2017, UNSW-NB15) focus on traffic classification and provide little structured information to support automatic rule synthesis or prevention logic. To address this gap, we propose Generative Thread Intelligence (GenTI) an LLM-driven benchmark for automatic generation of IDPS rules targeting unseen attacks. The dataset (GTI) aggregates over 150k detection and prevention rules from Snort, Suricata, Emerging Threats, as well as 50k YARA, each annotated with protocol behavior, payload signatures, contextual relationships, mappings to Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI), along with actionable response types (alert, drop, reject). Moreover, on top of this corpus we design an LLM-based pipeline that transforms analyst prompts and representative payloads into deployable rules via structured prompt engineering, Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, as well as a Chain-of-Verification (CoVe) loop for syntactic, semantic, and security validation. The generated rules are executed in real time on (Snort/Suricata) and evaluated by syntax accuracy, semantic similarity, CTI coverage, security effectiveness as well as unseen attacks detection. Furthermore, our GenTI instantiation achieves a composite rule-quality score of 89.4\%, with 94.8\% CTI coverage, improving unseen attacks detection from 45\% to 87.4\% and reducing the false-positive rate from 8.5\% to 2.3\%. Overall, GenTI establishes the first large-scale benchmark that tightly couples rule-level CTI with LLM-based automation, enabling adaptive, self-evolving IDPS.
tldr: This paper introduces GenTI, a benchmark and LLM-based pipeline for automatically generating IDPS rules to detect unseen attacks.
motivation: Existing rule-based IDPS systems rely on manually crafted signatures that fail against emerging and zero-day threats, and current datasets lack structured information for automatic rule synthesis.
method: The authors aggregate over 200k detection/prevention rules from Snort, Suricata, Emerging Threats, and YARA, annotate them with protocol behavior and CTI mappings, and design an LLM pipeline using prompt engineering, Chain-of-Thought reasoning, and Chain-of-Verification for rule generation and validation.
result: GenTI achieves a composite rule-quality score of 89.4%, 94.8% CTI coverage, improves unseen attack detection from 45% to 87.4%, and reduces false-positive rate from 8.5% to 2.3%.
conclusion: GenTI establishes a large-scale benchmark coupling rule-level CTI with LLM automation, enabling adaptive, self-evolving IDPS.

title: Metric Facility Assignment With Partial Information
authors: Vasilis Gkatzelis, Hasti Karimi, Emma Rewinski, Maziar Shamsipour, Alexandros A. Voudouris
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an assignment problem where a set of agents and a set of facilities lie on a line metric. The goal is to compute an assignment of agents to facilities to approximately minimize the social cost (the total distance of agents from their assigned facilities) given only partial information regarding the metric. Unlike previous work which focused solely on algorithms with access to the ordinal preferences of the agents over the facilities (ORD), we also consider the value of information regarding approval preferences (APP), and inter-facility distances (DIST). For different combinations of these three information types, we establish tight bounds on the distortion of deterministic algorithms, showing that it is possible to improve over the optimal bound of [MATH] that can be achieved using only ORD information. Among other results, we show a tight bound of [MATH] for APP+DIST which holds even for general metrics, and a tight bound of [MATH] for ORD+APP+DIST.
tldr: This paper studies metric facility assignment with partial information, focusing on distortion bounds for different information types.
motivation: To understand how limited information (ordinal preferences, approval preferences, inter-facility distances) affects the quality of facility assignment algorithms.
method: The authors analyze deterministic algorithms under various combinations of information types (ORD, APP, DIST) and prove tight distortion bounds.
result: They establish tight bounds, e.g., a bound of 3 for APP+DIST and a bound of 2 for ORD+APP+DIST, improving over the optimal bound using only ORD.
conclusion: The work provides a complete picture of achievable distortion under partial information, with implications for algorithmic mechanism design.

title: Double-Directional Wireless Channel Modeling Using Statistics-Aided Machine Learning
authors: Ferdous Pervej Richmond Boamah
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05993v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The double-directional (DD) wireless channel model is important for realistic system design since it provides complete propagation information. While stochastic and deterministic channel models are widely adopted, and existing machine learning (ML) solutions mostly aim to align future channel realizations, these solutions are often limited to short time spans that may not be statistically significant. Moreover, because the number of multi-path components (MPCs) varies with spatial and temporal variation of the receiver (RX) and/or interacting objects (IOs), typical ML solutions that require fixed, predefined input and output shapes fall short. To curb these limitations, we propose a statistics-aided ML solution that relies on a fixed subset of MPCs selection. More specifically, we first select top-[MATH] MPCs, where [MATH] is much smaller than the total number of MPCs, and construct learnable graphs to train our proposed hybrid TimesNet-TimeFilter (TNTF) model. We then use a channel statistics-aided training method to generate future top-M DD channel realizations such that the statistics calculated from these realizations matches closely with those of the actual statistics from the complete time-varying DD channel realizations. We validate the proposed solution using extensive simulations on both synthetic stochastic channel model (SCM)-based and deterministic ray-tracing-based datasets, and demonstrate its effectiveness relative to state-of-the-art baselines.
tldr: This paper proposes a statistics-aided machine learning model for double-directional wireless channel modeling, focusing on multi-path component selection and future channel realization generation.
motivation: Existing stochastic and deterministic channel models and ML solutions are limited by varying numbers of multi-path components and short time spans, motivating a need for a more flexible and statistically significant approach.
method: The authors select a fixed subset of top multi-path components, construct learnable graphs, and train a hybrid TimesNet-TimeFilter model using channel statistics-aided training to generate future channel realizations.
result: The proposed solution is validated on synthetic stochastic channel model and deterministic ray-tracing datasets, showing effectiveness compared to state-of-the-art baselines.
conclusion: The work provides a novel ML-based approach for double-directional channel modeling, but its relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is negligible.

title: RedEdit: Agentic Red-Teaming Of Image Safety Classifiers Via MCTS-Guided Photo-Editing
authors: Weilin Lin, Ziqi Lin, Zhenxing Zhou, Jianze Li, Tong Zhang, Hui Xiong, Li Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Image safety classifiers serve as a critical component of contemporary content moderation systems on the internet. However, their resilience against user-style malicious image editing remains underexplored. Such behaviors are highly prevalent in daily scenarios but difficult to fully reproduce. To explore this vulnerability, we introduce RedEdit, a novel black-box red-teaming agent that formulates photo-editing evasion as a combinatorial search problem over edit-tool sequences. It adopts a Vision-Language-Model (VLM)-based proposer to generate semantically targeted candidate edits and a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) planner to prioritize promising edit paths while backtracking from ineffective ones. Together, the proposer and planner instantiate two key capabilities of human attackers, i.e., domain knowledge and iterative backtracking, respectively, to reproduce this practical threat. Our extensive experiments on UnsafeBench reveal profound systemic vulnerabilities: fewer than two edits on average enable 76.2% of unsafe images to evade detectors, while retaining 93.0% malicious semantics, meaning that such manipulated content remains perceptually malicious to humans while easily bypassing automated moderation. We therefore appeal to the community for more attention to this overlooked practical threat.
tldr: This paper presents a red-teaming agent that uses MCTS and VLMs to generate adversarial image edits that evade safety classifiers.
motivation: To expose vulnerabilities in image safety classifiers against user-style malicious editing, which is common but underexplored.
method: A black-box agent combining a VLM-based proposer for candidate edits and MCTS for planning edit sequences.
result: With fewer than two edits on average, 76.2% of unsafe images evade detectors while retaining 93.0% malicious semantics.
conclusion: The work highlights a practical threat and calls for more attention to adversarial image editing in content moderation.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium decays and new hadron searches.
motivation: To understand strong interaction mechanisms like quark confinement and gluon binding through charmonium decays and searches for new hadrons.
method: Review of experimental results from BaBar, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII on hadron production in e+e- collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs.
result: BESIII has become the leading facility for high-precision measurements of hadron production in charm-meson pair systems.
conclusion: Continued experimental progress will provide deeper insights into QCD and hadron spectroscopy.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the scientific legacy of the Arecibo planetary radar system, focusing on observations of Solar System bodies and its role in planetary science.
motivation: To provide an overview of the Arecibo radar's contributions to planetary science, especially after its upgrade, and to highlight its unique capabilities for subsurface and surface characterization.
method: The paper is a review summarizing key observations and techniques of planetary radar, including delay-Doppler imaging and radar spectroscopy, applied to Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids.
result: Arecibo radar provided high-resolution images and compositional information of planetary surfaces and near-Earth asteroids, aiding in mission planning and hazard assessment.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar was a unique and powerful tool for planetary science; its loss leaves a gap that future radar systems may fill.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This colloquium reviews convection-cloud chambers as a tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds, focusing on droplet growth via condensation and collision coalescence.
motivation: The rapid transition from condensation to collision coalescence in warm clouds is poorly understood theoretically; the convection-cloud chamber offers controlled laboratory conditions to study this bottleneck.
method: The paper reviews experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches using convection-cloud chambers to reproduce turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation.
result: Key findings include insights into how convection-cloud chambers capture essential cloud processes and bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: The convection-cloud chamber is a promising tool for addressing the precipitation bottleneck, with implications for cloud physics and climate modeling.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews recent advances in nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions and their implications for stellar models.
motivation: To update the understanding of hydrogen-burning nuclear reactions in stars, which is crucial for predicting solar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work over the last decade, including plasma and atomic physics effects on nuclear reactions, and comparison with solar neutrino and helioseismic data.
result: Improved understanding of nuclear reaction rates and their impact on solar models, with new data refining predictions.
conclusion: The findings enhance the precision of solar interior models and may affect interpretations of solar neutrino experiments and stellar evolution.

title: Universal Deformations And Universal Residual Stresses In Incompressible Isotropic Cauchy Elasticity
authors: Arash Yavari
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study universal deformations in incompressible isotropic Cauchy elastic solids with residual stress, without assuming any specific origin for the residual stress. Starting from the constitutive representation of the Cauchy stress as an isotropic tensor-valued function of strain and residual stress, we derive the universality constraints for residually-stressed incompressible isotropic Cauchy elastic solids. We show that for the six known families of universal deformations the set of universal deformations is identical to that of incompressible isotropic elasticity in the absence of residual stress. We also show that residual stress does not enlarge the space of universal deformations. We then determine the universal residual stress fields corresponding to the six known families of universal deformations. Assuming that the residual stress field has the same symmetry as the corresponding universal deformation, the universality constraints reduce to systems of ordinary differential equations that can be solved explicitly. The resulting universal residual stress fields are characterized and discussed for each family.
tldr: This paper studies universal deformations and residual stresses in incompressible isotropic Cauchy elastic solids, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how residual stress affects universal deformations in nonlinear elasticity, without assuming a specific origin for the residual stress.
method: Derives universality constraints from constitutive representation of Cauchy stress as isotropic function of strain and residual stress, then solves ODEs for residual stress fields with symmetry assumptions.
result: The six known families of universal deformations remain unchanged by residual stress; universal residual stress fields are characterized for each family.
conclusion: Residual stress does not enlarge the space of universal deformations, and the derived residual stress fields can be used in further elasticity studies.

title: The Euclidean Algorithm, Lotuses And Singularities
authors: Patrick Popescu-Pampu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The anthyphairetic process leads from a pair (a,b) of coprime positive integers to the pair (1,1) by successive subtractions of the smaller number from the bigger one. This process, which is a slow version of Euclid's algorithm applied to the pair (a,b), corresponds naturally to the process of successive blowups leading to the minimal embedded resolution of the plane curve defined by y^a - x^b = 0. This blowup process may be represented graphically by a special two-dimensional simplicial complex called a lotus. This allows to localize the various numbers appearing either during the anthyphairetic process or during the Euclidean algorithm at precise positions inside the lotus. In this introductory article, I recall first the construction of this lotus starting from the sequence of quotients generated by the Euclidean algorithm. I present then an alternative way of constructing it directly from the sequence of pairs of coprime integers generated by the anthyphairetic process, using what I call anthyphairetic rectangles. I conclude by explaining how to reconstruct from a lotus the corresponding sequence of pairs of coprime integers. This is a simple illustration of the way lotuses may serve as computational architectures.
tldr: This paper explores the connection between the Euclidean algorithm, anthyphairetic process, and the minimal embedded resolution of plane curve singularities via a combinatorial structure called a lotus.
motivation: To provide an introductory exposition of how lotuses, derived from the Euclidean algorithm, serve as computational architectures for understanding singularities of plane curves.
method: The paper constructs lotuses from sequences of quotients in the Euclidean algorithm and from anthyphairetic rectangles, then shows how to recover the original coprime pairs from the lotus.
result: Lotuses can localize numbers from the Euclidean algorithm and anthyphairetic process, and they represent the blowup process for resolving the curve y^a - x^b = 0.
conclusion: Lotuses offer a visual and combinatorial tool for studying Euclidean algorithm and curve singularities, with potential applications in computational geometry.

The manuscript develops the basic theory of measurable sets, measurable functions, measures on [MATH]-algebras, Lebesgue integration, convergence theorems, and [MATH] spaces. Particular attention is devoted to the interaction between integration and convergence, as well as to the limitations of the Riemann integral that motivate the development of measure theory. The exposition seeks to balance mathematical rigor with pedagogical clarity through detailed proofs, examples, exercises, and supplementary projects. These notes are intended primarily for undergraduate students in mathematics and related areas encountering measure theory for the first time, although they may also serve as a reference for introductory graduate courses in analysis.
tldr: These notes provide an introduction to measure and integration theory, covering Lebesgue integration and convergence theorems.
motivation: To offer a rigorous yet accessible introduction to measure theory for undergraduate students, bridging the gap from Riemann to Lebesgue integration.
method: Pedagogical exposition with detailed proofs, examples, exercises, and supplementary projects.
result: Development of basic theory of measurable sets, functions, measures, Lebesgue integration, convergence theorems, and Lp spaces.

title: The {\alpha} -Discounting ({\alpha}-DMCDM) As An Extension Of Ahp, Topsis, Vikor, Promethee, And Weighted Sum
authors: Florentin Smarandache
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and other classic Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) techniques excel when decision makers can provide consistent pair wise judgments. Real world problems, however, often involve inconsistent, n-wise, or non-linear preference structures that render traditional methods inadequate. The {\alpha}-Discounting MCDM ({\alpha}-D MCDM) extends AHP by embedding a global discounting parameter {\alpha} that transforms an inconsistent system of preference equations into a solvable algebraic system.
tldr: This paper proposes an extension of multi-criteria decision making methods using a discounting parameter to handle inconsistent preferences.
motivation: Classic MCDM methods like AHP require consistent pairwise judgments, but real-world problems often involve inconsistent or non-linear preferences.
method: The α-Discounting MCDM embeds a global discounting parameter α to transform inconsistent preference equations into a solvable algebraic system.
result: The method extends AHP, TOPSIS, VIKOR, PROMETHEE, and weighted sum to handle inconsistent preferences.
conclusion: The approach provides a way to deal with real-world decision problems where traditional methods fail due to inconsistency.

title: The Ize Conjecture Redux: A Parity Criterion For Global Equivariant Bifurcation Guarantees
authors: Ziad Ghanem
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Ize Conjecture proposed that every absolutely irreducible representation of a compact Lie group admits a maximal isotropy subgroup with an odd-dimensional fixed-point space, which would provide a universal bifurcation guarantee via the equivariant degree. Its disproof by Lauterbach and Matthews necessitates a more targeted criterion. We introduce Ize pairs -- pairs [MATH] for which some maximal isotropy subgroup [MATH] satisfies [MATH] -- and prove that this dimension-parity condition completely captures the algebraic obstruction to a non-trivial equivariant degree change at maximal orbit types. Integrating this criterion with a mod-2 equivariant spectral flow yields local and global bifurcation guarantees without recourse to Burnside ring arithmetic. As an application, we establish unbounded branches of non-stationary periodic solutions in a [MATH]-symmetric coupled oscillator network, where the bifurcation guarantees follow entirely from the crossing parity of the linearization at the boundary of a regular parameter window.
tldr: This paper proves a parity criterion for global equivariant bifurcation in symmetric dynamical systems, with an application to coupled oscillator networks.
motivation: The Ize Conjecture was disproven, so a new criterion is needed to guarantee bifurcations in equivariant systems.
method: Introduces Ize pairs and combines a dimension-parity condition with mod-2 equivariant spectral flow to bypass Burnside ring arithmetic.
result: The parity condition completely captures the algebraic obstruction to nontrivial equivariant degree change at maximal orbit types, enabling local and global bifurcation guarantees.
conclusion: The criterion yields unbounded branches of non-stationary periodic solutions in a D4-symmetric oscillator network, demonstrating practical applicability.
